# generate-intent — Generation guide (Step 3 + 3.5)

## Contents
- Step 3 — Generate the 4 files (layout-2; conditional sections)
- Operator-workflow-UX capture + Design-Source OQ
- `vault.json` machine-readable manifest
- Reading the templates
- Step 3.5 — OQ auto-classification + halt YAML
- Project scale xs (size-weighted §2)
- Output mode policy
- Readability standards
- File-by-file content guide (vault/model/flows/constraints)
- Mandatory section template + OQ tagging
- constraints.md centralized Open Questions structure

## Step 3 — Generate the 4 files

Output to the **resolved output folder from Step 0** (`<OUTPUT_DIR>`). The layout-2 vault is **4 files** (SKILL body, The vault output contract): `vault.md` (frontmatter lock + `## Overview` / `## Architecture` / `## Decisions` — EXACT hard-header strings, see the template) · `model.md` · `flows.md` · `constraints.md` (+ script-derived `vault.json`). Vaults generated before v7 use the legacy 7-file layout (00–06); every reader is dual-layout for one minor cycle (`plugins/mega-sdd/references/paths.md §Vault layout`).

**Conditional sections** (driven by the Step 2 detection flags `HAS_UI_COMPONENTS` / `HAS_TOKENS` / `HAS_A11Y` / `HAS_VOICE_BRAND`):

- `vault.md ## Architecture > UI components & patterns` sub-section: appears **only if** `HAS_UI_COMPONENTS = true`. Otherwise omitted entirely (no header, no placeholder, no OQ).
- `constraints.md > Design system` section: appears **only if** at least one of `HAS_TOKENS`, `HAS_A11Y`, `HAS_VOICE_BRAND` is `true`. Within it, sub-blocks (Tokens / Accessibility / Voice & brand) appear only for the `true` flags.
- `vault.md ## Glossary`: product-specific PRD terms only. The generic + design-system standard rows (ADR, DBML, DoD, FK, NFR, OQ, RTO, RPO, SLO, design tokens, design system, WCAG, a11y, semantic HTML) live in the static `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md` (installed by the Step-3 `cp` of the shipped template) — never re-emitted per vault.

**No shape-based defaulting.** A `PROJECT_SHAPE=mobile-app` project with no source coverage of design-system content produces a vault with no design-system sections. The skill never injects WCAG levels, color palettes, spacing scales, or component lists from prior knowledge.

> Vault structure is the same regardless of `IMPLEMENTATION_MODE`. The mode flag lives in the vault.md frontmatter (`implementation_mode:`), not in the file count.

## Operator-workflow-UX capture + Design-Source OQ

> `validate-vault-oqs.sh` re-validates every vault doc write (PostToolUse) and surfaces a capture-stage miss as **advisory** via `analyze` (v4 Hybrid demoted this from a hard-block — it no longer blocks `mega-sdd:execute-bolts`). This prose is the real win — get it right at generation time.

**Rule 1 — model the operator surface when the flows show a workflow.** When the flows in `flows.md` exhibit a **maker-checker / multi-stage-approval / workflow** pattern (a user-facing flow with a maker→checker actor hand-off chain, OR ≥2 distinct decision transition steps — approve / reject / review / confirm), model the operator-facing surface as **FIRST-CLASS requirements GROUNDED in the flows** — never invented:

- **Worklist / inbox** — where each actor (checker, confirmer, …) finds the items awaiting *their* decision, filtered by role + current workflow state.
- **Decision affordance** — the approve / reject (and any return-to-prior-stage) actions available to the actor in the entity's current state.
- **Human-readable state labels** — a label map from the raw `workflow_state` enum to operator-facing text (e.g. `SUBMITTED` → "Awaiting Checker").
- **Audit timeline** — the append-only transition history rendered for the operator (who acted, when, prior → next state).

Capture these in `vault.md ## Architecture` (and the component/view inventory) and reflect them in `vault.json`. **Grounded, not invented:** every operator-surface requirement must trace to a flow step / actor / state in `flows.md`. If the surface design is genuinely undecided, capture it as an OQ instead of inventing it (Rule 2). The validator FAILs with `operator_surface_missing` when a workflow flow exists but the vault models no operator surface AND carries no Design-Source OQ.

> **Same workflow-flow signal also governs staging.** The maker→checker / multi-stage pattern that triggers operator-surface modeling here is also the staged-input pattern: if the source KB workflow carries a `## 3a` `stages:` block, PRESERVE it verbatim into this flow's `**Stages**` block + `_kb_source` per the flows.md generation step (`generate-intent/references/vault-core.md §stages-propagation`). Modeling the operator surface and preserving the staging are two halves of the same workflow fidelity — don't do one and flatten the other.

**Rule 2 — design system: template-first, then recommend, never a defaulted value.** When `HAS_UI_COMPONENTS = true` (UI components exist) but `HAS_TOKENS`, `HAS_A11Y`, and `HAS_VOICE_BRAND` are **all `false`** (no design source in PRD/Figma/KB), resolve the design system by **precedence** — never by silently defaulting WCAG levels, Material/Tailwind palettes, spacing scales, or brand voice from prior knowledge. (These three flags reflect the **PRD/Figma/KB source only**; a scanned starterkit is a SEPARATE input, evaluated in path 1 below — so this rule still fires when the PRD has no design source even though a template was scanned.)

1. **Scanned template wins (source: `scanned-template`).** If a starterkit was scanned and `starterkit-context.yaml §ui_ux` supplies a design system (`design_tokens` / `layout_extends` / `idioms`), DERIVE `design_system` from the template — its flow is authoritative. **ui-ux-pro-max does NOT recommend a style here; it must not override or contradict the template.** Emit a Design-Source OQ ONLY for a genuine gap the template is silent on (e.g. a missing chart palette), and that gap-fill OQ must align with template idioms. Write `design_system` with `source: scanned-template`, `provenance` citing the `starterkit-context.yaml §ui_ux` anchor.

2. **Greenfield — recommend (source: `design-intelligence-recommend`).** ONLY when there is no scanned template design system (true greenfield / `--greenfield`), emit a single high-priority **Design-Source Open Question** `OQ-DESIGN-SOURCE-{N} [P1]` with `resolution_mode: recommend` (NOT a silent default — see vault-core.md §OQ schema). Consult `plugins/mega-sdd/references/design-intelligence/product-style-map.yaml` using PRD signals (product type, industry, brand hints):
   - `recommendation`: the chosen `{style, palette, typography, a11y_level}` from the matched `product-style-map` entry (the map key is `a11y_baseline` — write it into the vault as `a11y_level`).
   - `rationale`: the PRD signal → matched map key (e.g. "product_type=SaaS dashboard (PRD §1) → product-style-map.yaml#saas-general").
   - `scan_citations`: `["plugins/mega-sdd/references/design-intelligence/product-style-map.yaml#<key>", "<PRD §>"]` — **never fabricate**; if no map entry matches, fall back to a bare `resolution_mode: blocking` OQ instead.
   - `fallback_if_wrong`: "blocking — request an explicit design source from the PO".
   Only when the user accepts is the `design_system` block written (with `source: design-intelligence-recommend`).

In both cases the `design_system` block (vault-contract.md §design_system) is written into the authored patch (it lands in `vault.json` via `derive-vault-json.sh`) + the `constraints.md > Design system` section, each line cited to its source. The validator still FAILs with `design_source_oq_missing` when UI components exist with all three design flags false and **no** Design-Source OQ (blocking or recommend) is present AND no scanned-template design system was derived.

## `vault.json` machine-readable manifest

Alongside the 4 markdown files, `vault.json` is a structured manifest AI dev consumers (Claude Code, Cursor, automated agents) load for fast, reliable context without parsing prose markdown. Markdown remains the human-authoritative source; JSON is a derived index. **The model NEVER writes `vault.json`** — it is script-derived:

- **Run** `bash $PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/derive-vault-json.sh --vault <OUTPUT_DIR> --patch <patch-file>` at Step 3.8 — after `constitution.md` (Step 3.4) and the Step-3.5 classifier complete, so the authored patch carries their records and `constitution.md` is on disk for the hash pin. The script derives every structural mirror from the markdown: `entities[]`, `flows[]`, `adrs[]`, `open_questions[]` skeletons, `open_questions_summary`, `vault_version` + the six Vault Lock enums (incl. the optional `project_scale`); it computes `constitution_hash` fresh at initial generation and carries it forward thereafter.
- **The model still authors** (via the `--patch` JSON, a scratchpad temp file): `title`, `source_documents`, `design_system_flags` [+ `design_system`], scope block (`scope`/`scope_metadata`/`prd_sha256`/`prd_path_at_generation`), `phase`/`phase_total`, and the per-OQ JSON-only classifier fields (`scan_query`, `recommendation`, `rationale`, `scan_citations`, `fallback_if_wrong`). Setting a derived key in the patch exits 2 (anti-laundering).
- **Lock:** the script acquires and releases `<vault>/vault.json.lock` itself (backoff + retry per `generate-intent/references/vault-contract.md §Concurrency contract`); exit 4 → surface the existing `memory_in_use` halt envelope.
- **Schema, field rules, and regeneration trigger points** → `generate-intent/references/vault-contract.md §schema`.
- **Why both formats:** humans review markdown (narrative, citations, nuance); AI consumers read `vault.json` (fast structural lookup, no token-heavy prose parsing, reliable enum-based status/priority filtering).

## Reading the templates

Use templates in `references/templates/` as scaffolds. **Resolve the path relative to where the skill is mounted:**

- **Claude Code (plugin install — primary distribution):** read `$PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/generate-intent/references/templates/<name>.md`, where `$PLUGIN_ROOT` resolves to the **LATEST cached version** (not whatever version path happens to be in context — that may be stale; see `plugins/mega-sdd/references/plugin-root-resolution.md`). Resolve it with one Bash call before reading templates:
  ```bash
  DERIVED="<this reference file's absolute path, truncated before /skills/>"
  RESOLVER="$(ls -1 ~/.claude/plugins/cache/mega-sdd/mega-sdd/*/scripts/resolve-plugin-root.sh 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
  PLUGIN_ROOT="$([ -n "$RESOLVER" ] && bash "$RESOLVER" "$DERIVED" || echo "$DERIVED")"
  [ -n "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ] || PLUGIN_ROOT="$DERIVED"; echo "$PLUGIN_ROOT"
  ```
- **Claude Code (manual install at `~/.claude/skills/`):** `~/.claude/skills/generate-intent/references/templates/<name>.md`
- **Claude Code (project-scoped manual install):** `<project-root>/.claude/skills/generate-intent/references/templates/<name>.md`
- **Claude.ai upload:** `/mnt/skills/user/generate-intent/references/templates/<name>.md`

Read the relevant template (Claude Code: `Read` tool; Claude.ai sandbox: `view` / platform read tool), then fill it in based on extracted facts. **Never invent fields beyond what the source PRD/Figma supports.**

## Step 3.5 — OQ auto-classification

After Step 3 writes the 4 files but BEFORE the Step 4 self-check, run the auto-classifier on every generated OQ (they all live in `constraints.md ## Open Questions`):

1. **For each OQ in `constraints.md ## Open Questions`**, apply the heuristic table from `generate-intent/references/vault-contract.md §Auto-classifier heuristics`: match the OQ text against the pattern column; assign `category`, `resolution_mode`, `classification_confidence`. Conservative default when no pattern matches: `category: business`, `resolution_mode: blocking`, `classification_confidence: low`.
2. **For `resolution_mode: scan`:** populate `scan_query` from the OQ's "Resolves:" hint or infer the codebase-map section to probe (e.g., "what test framework?" → `scan_query: "codebase-map §test_frameworks"`).
3. **For `resolution_mode: recommend`:** populate the four required fields:
   - `recommendation` — Claude's pick (1–2 sentences).
   - `rationale` — why this pick; what trade-off was considered (2–3 sentences).
   - `scan_citations` — at least 1 entry; cite a related-pattern anchor in the codebase-map / KB / source PRD (e.g., `app/Http/Resources/ErrorResource.php:12`). If no exact match exists, cite the closest pattern with a "no exact match; closest: …" note.
   - `fallback_if_wrong` — what to revisit if this recommendation turns out incorrect (1 sentence).
   - **Anti-halu rail:** NEVER fabricate citations. If no codebase context exists at all, downgrade to `category: business` with note "no codebase context to ground recommendation; needs human decision."
4. **For `resolution_mode: blocking`** (default for business + low-confidence tech): no additional fields required.
4b. **`project_scale: xs` defer-by-default (size-weighted §2, 7.29.0).** When the vault frontmatter carries `project_scale: xs`: every **tech** OQ (`scan`/`recommend`) with `classification_confidence: medium` is BORN deferred — annotate the markdown entry with `**Deferred**: project_scale=xs — auto-deferred at generation; resolves at binding (brownfield) / resurfaces via resolve-oq (greenfield), tidak ditanya interaktif` and carry `defer_to` for it in the authored patch — `binding` when the vault is brownfield (`implementation_mode: existing` AND repo signals present — the only context where a binding target is legal, per `resolve-oq/references/interactive-walk.md §Defer targets`), otherwise `stakeholder` (greenfield — the same value the express auto-defer writes; amended 7.29.1). These OQs are listed in §Auto-Classification Review under an `Auto-deferred (project_scale: xs)` sub-heading and are NEVER surfaced in an interactive walk (resolve-oq's priority walk and the chain's batched-P1 walk both skip `deferred`). **The evidence standard is unchanged:** `high`-confidence auto-resolve still requires the same citation probe at bind time; what changes is ASK vs DEFER, never the proof. Business OQs and `low`-confidence tech (conservative-default → business/blocking) are untouched — human-decided as always.
5. **Write classified OQ data** back to the markdown body (the `[tech / scan]` / `[conf: …]` brackets + resolve hints) and put the JSON-only fields into the authored patch consumed by `derive-vault-json.sh`, per `generate-intent/references/vault-contract.md §Updated OQ schema` — never hand-edit `vault.json`.
6. **Generate the `vault.md` "## Auto-Classification Review" section.** List every tech-tagged OQ + every flipped/manually-overridden OQ. Only `high`-confidence tech OQs auto-resolve downstream in `bind-codebase`; `medium`/`low` are flagged for user review.
7. **Validation gate:** before proceeding to Step 4, validate every OQ entry per `generate-intent/references/vault-contract.md §Validation rules`:
   - Tech OQ missing `resolution_mode` → halt `oq_tech_missing_mode`.
   - `recommend` OQ missing any of `recommendation`, `rationale`, `scan_citations`, `fallback_if_wrong` → halt `oq_recommend_underspecified`.
   - `scan` OQ missing `scan_query` → halt `oq_scan_missing_query`.

**Halt YAML format:**

```yaml
blocker:
  type: oq_recommend_underspecified
  emitted_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>
  emitted_by: generate-intent
  details:
    oq_id: OQ-AR-7
    missing_fields: [scan_citations, fallback_if_wrong]
    oq_text: "<verbatim from vault>"
  next_action: "Re-run generate-intent OR populate the missing fields in the authored patch and re-run derive-vault-json.sh before bind-codebase."
```

## Project scale xs (size-weighted §2)

Set by Step 2 from `scripts/derive-project-scale.sh` (deterministic structure count; greenfield lanes only — KB sub-mode and `--scan` overlays are always `standard`). At `project_scale: xs` exactly TWO things change; nothing else:

1. **`vault.md ## Glossary` is omitted** (no header, no placeholder — the omit-never-fabricate rail) — the parser treats it as optional and `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md §Standard terms` already carries the generic rows. Every other section keeps its normal rules: the conditional sections (`HAS_*` design blocks, API contracts) are already source-gated, the three hard-header H2 anchors stay mandatory, and `## Changelog`/`## Phase context` stay (they have writers/readers).
2. **Step 3.5 rule 4b** — medium-confidence tech OQs are born deferred (`defer_to: binding` in brownfield, `stakeholder` in greenfield — the `defer_to` contract), recorded in §Auto-Classification Review, never asked interactively.

The target class: a "3 static screens" PRD stops producing a wall of interactive questions — OQ COUNT is unchanged (honesty), the interactive ceremony shrinks. `xs` can only ever come from structural evidence in the source document; absent/unparseable structure means `standard`.

## Output mode policy

Driven by `OUTPUT_MODE` (Step 0.7):

| Aspect | `compact` (default) | `full` |
|--------|---------------------|--------|
| TL;DR header (doc 01–06) | 1 line: `> **TL;DR**: <doc summary> · <intended audience> · <when to read>.` | 3 lines (TL;DR / Audience / When to read) |
| API contracts (doc 02) | Table: endpoint · method · purpose · auth · errors · source. Skip request/response JSON unless the payload is non-trivial or has a nested struct that isn't obvious from field names. | Full request/response JSON example per endpoint |
| Entity descriptions (doc 03) | DBML only + 1-line `Purpose:` per entity. No prose narrative. | DBML + per-entity prose: Purpose, Key fields, Relations |
| Flow blocks (doc 04) | Mermaid flowchart (the flow body) + DoD checklist per flow. Skip Preconditions/Postconditions sections (derivable from the diagram). Source line still required. | Actor / Trigger + Preconditions + Mermaid flow diagram + Postconditions + DoD + Failure handling + Source |
| Decision blocks (doc 05) | 1-paragraph: `D-XXX: title — context in 1 sentence. Decision: <X>. Consequences: <Y, Z>. Source: PRD §...` | Multi-section: Status / Date / Context / Decision / Consequences (✅⚠️ bullets) / Source |
| Glossary (doc 00) | Product-specific PRD terms only + the pointer line to `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md` §Standard terms. | Same — the generic-rows drop is unconditional (both modes); the static guide carries the standard rows |
| Open Questions per doc | 1-line: `OQ-{CODE}-{N} [P{1\|2\|3}]: <question> — resolve: <PIC/source>` | Multi-line: question + reasoning + impact + resolution path |
| Sources section | Bullet list, no prose intro. | Same |
| "Note" / "Why X" asides in body | Cut. Reasoning belongs in `vault.md ## Decisions`. | Allowed when it adds context. |
| Cross-ref to other doc | 1 anchor link, no quote duplication. | Inline quote of cited doc allowed. |

**Hard invariants — preserved in BOTH modes:** every claim cites a source (PRD §, Figma frame, uploaded file); every OQ tagged `OQ-{CODE}-{N}` with priority `P1|P2|P3`; every flow has a Definition of Done as an observable checklist; every decision has an explicit source; Out of Scope never empty (`TBD - confirm with PO` if genuinely unknown).

**Audience principle:** `compact` = optimized for builder reading (architect, dev, QA) — tables + DoD + citations, skips narrative scaffolding because the reader knows the domain. `full` = optimized for cross-functional review (PM, BO, legal, compliance + builder) — prose context for non-technical readers, examples for clarity.

**Doc 04 (flows) exception:** `compact` still cuts Preconditions/Postconditions, but the Mermaid flow diagram + DoD detail stay complete (flow correctness > token saving for QA & implementation); `full` uses full structured blocks per template.

Cut filler. No padding to look thorough. No amputation to look minimal. Output mode adjusts the **granularity of context**, not the completeness of facts.

## Readability standards (mandatory for all 4 files)

**Output language convention** (generated docs match the input PRD language):
- Code-level terms always in English: entity names (`mega_rencana_account`), field names (`source_account_id`), types (`bigint`, `varchar`), enum values (`active | dormant`), HTTP methods, protocol names, framework names.
- Prose narrative in the PRD's language. Don't mix English and the PRD language in one prose sentence except to reference a code term.
- Avoid awkward hybrid phrasing. Indonesian PRD example: ❌ "Status MUST be active" → ✅ "Status harus `active`".
- Avoid direct-translating from AC verbatim: ❌ "Sistem dapat melakukan pembayaran full akumulasi autodebet dan rekening tidak ditutup" → ✅ "Sistem bayar full akumulasi → rekening tetap aktif."

**Anti-AI-tone:** read each paragraph aloud mentally; if it sounds like AI translation or robotic prose, rewrite it in natural conversational tone for the target language. Avoid excessive hedging ("could", "may", "possibly") unless the content is genuinely ambiguous (then it goes to OQs). Use active, short, direct sentences.

**Placement discipline:** Every generated artifact leads with its densest load-bearing content — TL;DR, verdict/OQ counts, markers, citations, DoD, hard constraints — and pushes exposition, glossary, and append-only history to the tail. LLM consumers weight the start and end of a document most; the middle is the weakest position. Never let a growing history section or generic boilerplate occupy the opening region, and never dilute a load-bearing table with narrative between its header and its rows. Summaries with counts go first; anything a reader could skip goes last.

**Glossary policy:** first-use acronym/jargon in any doc → define it inline at first occurrence (e.g., "DBML (Database Markup Language)"). `vault.md` MUST have a **Glossary** section (EXCEPT at `project_scale: xs`, where the section is omitted entirely — §Project scale xs) carrying **product-specific PRD terms only** (e.g., MPIN, CIF, OTP, parameterized) plus one pointer line to the **Standard terms** table in `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md`. Never re-emit the generic rows (ADR, DBML, DoD, FK, NFR, OQ, RTO, RPO, SLO, or the design-system terms) into vault.md — they ship in the static guide, both output modes.

**Cross-reference budget:** max 2 cross-refs to other section/doc per section. If more are needed, inline the essential information or move to an appendix. Cross-refs must be self-contained.

**Date format convention:** `Last updated:` → `YYYY-MM-DD`; decision dates, PRD versions, sprint/milestone refs → `YYYY-MM`.

**Per-doc TL;DR (mandatory: the vault.md `## Overview`/`## Architecture` sections + model.md, flows.md, constraints.md)** — format depends on `OUTPUT_MODE`:

```markdown
# OUTPUT_MODE=compact (default) — 1 line:
> **TL;DR**: <doc summary> · <primary audience> · <when to read this>.

# OUTPUT_MODE=full — 3 lines:
> **TL;DR**: <one sentence: what this doc contains>.
> **Audience**: <primary reader role, e.g. Architect / Dev / QA / PM>.
> **Read when**: <condition for relevance, e.g. "you're reviewing system structure">.
```

> TL;DR placeholders shown in English for clarity. At runtime, render them in the PRD's language.

1. **Project header** — `# <Project Name> — Grand Design` + 1-sentence description.

1.5. **Phase context** — emit immediately after the header:

2. **`## Overview`** — what the 01 doc used to carry: Product (2–3 sentences) · Target users/personas (PRD-named only) · Problem · Success criteria (PRD-sourced, else an OQ in constraints.md). Section tail: `### Sources` + `### Out of Scope` (H3 — the H2 tails belong to the standalone files).
3. **`## Architecture`** — what the 02 doc used to carry: System overview (1 paragraph + text diagram) · per-layer sub-sections derived from `PROJECT_SHAPE` (each role deep-links `vault.md#<layer-anchor>`) · conditional `#### UI components & patterns` (`HAS_UI_COMPONENTS=true` only) · API contracts (`compact`: table per group; `full`: JSON per endpoint) · Tech stack per layer. Tail: `### Sources` + `### Out of Scope`.
4. **`## Decisions`** — ADR-lite `### D-NNN:` entries, format per `OUTPUT_MODE` (see the template). Only decisions with an explicit source; PRD silent → an OQ in constraints.md, never an ADR.
5. **`## Glossary`** — product-specific PRD terms only + the pointer line to `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md` §Standard terms. Omitted entirely at `project_scale: xs` (§Project scale xs).
6. **`## Auto-Classification Review`** — written by Step 3.5 (tech-tagged + flipped OQs).
7. **`## Source documents`** — files consumed (PRD provenance).
8. **`## Changelog`** — append-only version history (newest first), at the TAIL — history must never push load-bearing content out of the opening region.
9. **`## Last updated`** — YYYY-MM-DD.

> The legacy 00-index ceremony (Executive Summary mirror, Project Readiness table, Reading paths/order, generic anti-hallucination restatement, OQ roll-up) is NOT emitted in layout-2 — the generic protocol lives in `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md`, the OQ universe lives in constraints.md + vault.json.

### model.md
- **TL;DR header** · default format **DBML** — per entity: `// Purpose:` comment (machine-read into `entities[].purpose`), key fields + types, relations with FK direction, constraints. `compact`: DBML + 1-line Purpose only; `full`: + per-entity prose. NO Open Questions section (centralized).

### flows.md
> **Exception to the simplicity policy:** this doc is allowed to be reasonably complete.

- **TL;DR header** · **By flow type** — sub-sections derived from `PROJECT_SHAPE`. For each flow: the flow body is a **Mermaid flowchart** — never a prose numbered Steps list (Mermaid-flows hard rule; each entry MUST carry a ` ```mermaid ` block or `validate-kb.sh --surface=vault-flows` FAILs it). Staged inputs (multi-step workflows): PRESERVE the KB `stages:` block verbatim + Mermaid `stateDiagram` + `_kb_source` per `vault-contract.md §stages-propagation` — never flatten. Cross-cutting flows show handoffs inside the Mermaid diagram (`subgraph` per layer). NO Open Questions section (centralized — use `[origin: flows.md#F-<prefix>-NNN]`).

### constraints.md
- **TL;DR header** · Technical constraints · Business constraints · **NFR table** (| Category | Requirement | Source |) · conditional **Design system** section (flags-driven) · **`## Open Questions` — THE one authored OQ surface** (structure below).

```markdown
- Figma: <frame-name or URL fragment>

## Out of Scope

- <if unknown: "TBD - confirm with PO">
```

**NO per-doc Open Questions section** — every OQ lives in constraints.md (below). **Open Question tagging convention:** see `generate-intent/references/vault-contract.md §OQ-conventions` for the tag format, topic-prefix table, and priority definitions.

## constraints.md centralized Open Questions structure

ALL OQs live in ONE `## Open Questions` section in constraints.md (`derive-vault-json.sh` exits 2 on an OQ checkbox line in any other doc). Sort P1 → P2 → P3. Every non-constraints-native OQ carries `[origin: <file>#<anchor>]` naming where the question arose; the `[tech / <mode>]` / `[business]` bracket is MANDATORY (bracket-first is the only category source — there is no roll-up fallback).

```markdown
- [ ] **OQ-CN-1** [P2] [business]: <constraints-native — no origin>
```

- Path mismatch with environment (alien path) → reject per Step 0 rules.
- Output folder exists and non-empty → ask before overwriting.

### Only when `PRD_STATUS=draft`
- Inputs missing critical sections (e.g. no flows in the PRD) → ask before generating.
- PRD is contradictory → surface contradictions in chat, ask which version is canonical, wait for resolution.
- Gap count > 10 → ask whether to proceed or get clarification first.

### Only when `PRD_STATUS=final`
- Do NOT pause for any of the three `draft` cases above. PRD is locked, stakeholder is unavailable for synchronous clarification.
- Missing sections, contradictions, large gaps → all funnel into the Open Questions roll-up with full context (quotes from the PRD, what's missing, what would resolve it).
- For contradictions specifically: write the OQ as `OQ-{DOC}-{N} [P1]: PRD inconsistency — §X.Y says "<quote A>" but §X.Z says "<quote B>". Need stakeholder ruling on which is canonical.`
- Surface in the Step 5 summary: total OQ count + reminder that the user must triage with the stakeholder before dev starts.

### Design-system absence is acceptable (no push-back)
Design-system content is **auxiliary**. Source silence on tokens, UI components, a11y, or brand voice is allowed and produces vault output without those sections. The skill MUST NOT:
- Prompt the user "do you have a Figma URL / tokens file / Storybook export?"
- Default to industry standards (WCAG 2.1 AA, Material Design, iOS HIG, Tailwind defaults).
- Generate placeholder Open Questions for missing design-system content.

If the user explicitly mentions a design system in conversation but didn't upload a source, treat that as a regular request for clarification (one chat question), not a workflow gate. Otherwise stay silent.

95:## OQ authoring — human-first (mandat tim, 2026-09-02)
96-
97-§Register mengatur register (kaku vs natural); section ini mengatur **komprehensibilitas** — keluhan lapangan: "bahasa OQ seperti alien". Berlaku untuk SEMUA teks OQ yang DITULIS ke artifact (KB PRD-kontrak §6, vault `constraints.md ## Open Questions`, propagasi binding):
98-
99-Setiap OQ = **pertanyaan utuh yang bisa dijawab orang bisnis TANPA buka kode**, tiga bagian berurutan:
100-1. Satu kalimat konteks situasi dalam bahasa manusia (kapan/di mana masalah ini muncul).
101-2. Pertanyaannya sendiri — jargon internal (nama SP, kolom, simbol, config key) BOLEH sebagai penjelas dalam kurung, **TIDAK BOLEH jadi subjek kalimat**.
102-3. Detail teknis (sitasi `file:line`, marker) menyusul sebagai keterangan.
103-
104-| ❌ Alien (jangan) | ✅ Manusiawi (tulis begini) |
105-|---|---|
106-| `OQ-ACQ-03 [P1] grace_period NULL fallback semantics SP_CALC_DENDA?` | `OQ-ACQ-03 [P1] Kalau jatuh tempo lewat tapi masa tenggang belum diisi (kolom grace_period kosong — SP_CALC_DENDA:120), denda mulai dihitung dari hari ke berapa? [OPEN][?]` |
107-
108-Tag/ID/marker tetap Tier-1 (English verbatim, tak berubah) — yang diatur section ini hanya BADAN teks pertanyaannya. Aturan yang sama berlaku untuk teks jawaban/hasil yang direkam (resolution answers, rationale): tulis buat pembaca bisnis dulu, detail teknis menyusul.
109-
110-## Switching & extensibility
111-
112-- Default `id` (carried by the anchor + the greenfield entry-point directives). The user says "use English" / "pakai bahasa Inggris" / "pakai bahasa Jawa" → the model mirrors.
113-- Any language works with zero new code: the model is multilingual and Tier-1 stays English regardless. No catalog, no per-language code.
114-- Not persistent across sessions (and re-asserted each session/compaction by the anchor) — by design, the lightest-touch config.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# derive-vault-json.sh — deterministic generator (W5): <vault>/vault.json is
# DERIVED from the 7 vault markdown files, never hand-written or model-emitted.
# HYBRID three-lane contract (spec 2026-07-19-batch2-derive-and-diet.md, W5):
#   DERIVE lane        — structural mirrors from md (entities / flows / adrs /
#                        open_questions skeletons / summary / Vault Lock enums).
#                        md is authoritative for existence — EXCEPT entries
#                        carrying defer_to: binding (no md home; preserved+WARN).
#   CARRY-FORWARD lane — at-generation pins (prd_sha256, prd_path_at_generation,
#                        constitution_hash/constitution_version, legacy mode,
#                        scope/scope_metadata/title, …) + EVERY prior key the
#                        deriver does not own, verbatim (unknown-key tolerance).
#   PATCH lane         — --patch <file.json>: model-authored values only
#                        (metadata, source_documents, design_system_flags,
#                        legacy advisor (carried), per-OQ scan_query/recommendation/rationale/
#                        scan_citations/fallback_if_wrong/defer_to). Setting a
#                        derived key exits 2 (anti-laundering).
#   --event '<json>'   — append ONE changelog event under the same lock
#                        (bind Step 6, resolve-oq round events).
# Shares its md grammar with validate-vault-oqs.sh via _lib/vault_md.py
# (two-validators-one-grammar; the W2 binding_md.py precedent).
# constitution_hash/constitution_version are CARRIED FORWARD like prd_sha256
# (at-generation pin; recompute would silently re-baseline a hand-edited
# constitution) — computed fresh ONLY when absent (initial generation); a WARN
# fires when the carried hash differs from the current constitution.md (free
# drift advisory — the enforced halt stays binding.md-anchored in detect-drift).
# run-analyze.sh's entities/OQ count-sync checks stay UNTOUCHED as independent
# loose-parse cross-checks of this deriver.
# Exit 0 = derived (ONE PASS line; WARNs to stderr); 2 = derive/parse/patch
# error, vault.json NOT written — on an md-grammar mismatch: mega-sdd-authored
# docs = an authoring bug (fix the markdown write and re-run); externally-
# authored vault docs = not a bug, the grammar was never adopted (v5 adoption
# lane) — fix manually per the generate-intent templates or re-generate via
# the pipeline; 3 = usage / unreadable vault; 4 =
# vault.json.lock held after backoff (skill maps to the memory_in_use halt —
# keterangan envelope stays at the skill layer, verbatim).
set -u
VAULT=""; PATCH=""; EVENT=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in
  --vault) VAULT="$2"; shift 2;; --vault=*) VAULT="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --patch) PATCH="$2"; shift 2;; --patch=*) PATCH="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  --event) EVENT="$2"; shift 2;; --event=*) EVENT="${1#*=}"; shift;;
  *) shift;; esac; done
[ -n "$VAULT" ] || { echo "usage: derive-vault-json.sh --vault <dir> [--patch <file.json>] [--event '<json>']" >&2; exit 3; }
[ -d "$VAULT" ] || { echo "FAIL: vault dir not found: $VAULT" >&2; exit 3; }
# Dual-layout identity (v7 Fase 3, one minor cycle): layout-2 vault.md OR the
# legacy 00-index.md — one of the two is mandatory.
if [ ! -f "$VAULT/vault.md" ] && [ ! -f "$VAULT/00-index.md" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: neither $VAULT/vault.md (layout-2) nor $VAULT/00-index.md (legacy) exists — not a vault" >&2; exit 3
fi
if [ -n "$PATCH" ] && [ ! -f "$PATCH" ]; then echo "FAIL: --patch file not found: $PATCH" >&2; exit 3; fi
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
export MEGA_SDD_LIB_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/_lib"

V_VAULT="$VAULT" V_PATCH="$PATCH" V_EVENT="$EVENT" python3 <<'PYEOF'
import hashlib, json, os, re, sys, time
from datetime import datetime, timezone

sys.path.insert(0, os.environ["MEGA_SDD_LIB_DIR"])
import vault_md

vault = os.environ["V_VAULT"]
patch_path = os.environ.get("V_PATCH") or ""
event_raw = os.environ.get("V_EVENT") or ""
js_path = os.path.join(vault, "vault.json")
lock_path = os.path.join(vault, "vault.json.lock")

# Layout-aware doc set (v7 Fase 3 dual read, one minor cycle). LAYOUT2 keys
# every branch below; DOCS keeps each layout's file list, DOC_* name the doc
# that owns each structural class in the active layout.
LAYOUT2 = vault_md.is_layout2_vault(vault)
if LAYOUT2:
    DOCS = ["vault.md", "model.md", "flows.md", "constraints.md"]
    DOC_INDEX, DOC_DM, DOC_FL, DOC_DC = "vault.md", "model.md", "flows.md", "vault.md"
    OQ_DOCS = ["constraints.md"]         # OQs are centralized — sole authored home
else:
    DOCS = ["00-index.md", "01-overview.md", "02-architecture.md",
            "03-data-model.md", "04-flows.md", "05-decisions.md",
            "06-constraints.md"]
    DOC_INDEX, DOC_DM, DOC_FL, DOC_DC = ("00-index.md", "03-data-model.md",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# validate-constitution.sh — R5: constitution enforcement validator.
#
# Walking-skeleton scope:
#   1. Check constitution.md exists in active vaults
#   2. Compute sha256 of constitution.md
#   3. Check handoff-validation-state.json carries matching constitution_hash (if present)
#   4. Check binding.md references constitution clauses (section headers)
#   5. Check unit files reference constitution clauses via binding_refs or Hard Rules
#
# Inputs: --cwd=<project> [--quiet]
# Outputs: <cwd>/.mega-sdd/.constitution-state.json
# Exit: 0=PASS/SKIP, 1=FAIL, 2=error

set -uo pipefail

CWD=""
QUIET=0

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --cwd=*) CWD="${arg#--cwd=}" ;;
    --quiet) QUIET=1 ;;
  esac
done
# Resolve project root (Iter 71 — class-bug fix: if invoked from a sub-folder
# like .mega-sdd/knowledge-base/, walk UP to the outermost .mega-sdd/ parent
# so state files land in the canonical location, not nested .mega-sdd/.mega-sdd/).
_RPR_HELPER="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)/_lib/resolve-project-root.sh"
if [ -f "$_RPR_HELPER" ] && [ -n "${CWD:-}" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  . "$_RPR_HELPER"
  CWD=$(resolve_project_root "$CWD")
fi


if [ -z "$CWD" ]; then CWD="$(pwd)"; fi
if [ ! -d "${CWD}/.mega-sdd" ]; then exit 2; fi

STATE_FILE="${CWD}/.mega-sdd/.constitution-state.json"
_LIB_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)/_lib"

RESULT=$(CWD="$CWD" _LIB_DIR="$_LIB_DIR" python3 <<'PYEOF'
import json
import os

# Clinic Appointment System — Grand Design (CLINIC)

> Online appointment booking for one small clinic: patients self-book, reschedule and cancel without calling; doctors and receptionists manage the daily schedule.

**Scope**: Clinic Web App (`CLINIC`)
**PICs**: Engineering Lead, Design Lead
**Priority**: 1 (delivery sequencing hint)
**PRD source**: `PRD/prd-clinic.md` (sha256: `34b026c22edebce30d2d5853edc5f8a58a3349891df4f96e482ed9f1e6465d0a`)
**Universal sections included**: §1, §2, §3, §4, §5, §6, §7, §8, §9
**Scope-specific section**: §Clinic

**Sibling scopes**: none — single-scope PRD. **Locked contracts published / consumed**: none (PRD `cross_scope_dependencies: []`).

> Generic AI-consumer protocol (how to read this vault, halt handling, standard terms): `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md`.

## Phase context

**Phase:** 1 of 1

**Project type:** single-phase

## Overview

> **TL;DR**: What the clinic booking product is, who uses it, and how success is measured · PO, architect, QA · read first.

### Product

A web app for one clinic (5 doctors, ~50 appointments/day) where patients book, reschedule and cancel appointments online, and staff see and manage the daily schedule. Automated email reminders 24 hours ahead aim to cut no-shows. The UI must be accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA).

### Target users / personas

- **Patient**: books, reschedules and cancels their own appointments; no login — cancel/reschedule via a one-time email token (PRD §3).
- **Doctor**: staff role; views their own schedule (PRD §3).
- **Receptionist**: staff role; views all schedules, manages conflicts, creates walk-in/phone appointments (PRD §3).
- **Product Owner / clinic staff**: own rollout and success metrics (PRD §3).

### Problem

Bookings happen by phone (~5 min of staff time each) and the no-show rate is 18%. Patients cannot self-serve, and staff lack an at-a-glance schedule (PRD §1, §2).

### Success criteria

- ≥ 50% of appointments booked online within 3 months, measured via `booking_channel` (PRD §2, §9, BR-006).
- No-show rate < 10% within 3 months, baseline 18% (PRD §2, §9) — measurement method open: OQ-OV-2.
- Median staff time per booking < 30 s, down from ~5 min (PRD §2, §9) — measurement method open: OQ-OV-3.
- WCAG 2.2 AA across the UI (PRD §2, §6.1).

### Sources

- PRD §1, §2, §3, §9

### Out of Scope

- Multi-clinic support · payment processing (price display only) · SMS reminders · patient medical records · recurring appointments · multi-language UI (English only) · patient login/accounts (PRD §7).

## Architecture

> **TL;DR**: One Next.js full-stack app — public patient surfaces, role-gated staff surfaces, a reminder cron endpoint, Postgres storage, email integration · architect, devs · read before designing any unit.

### System overview

A single Next.js 16 (App Router) app serves both audiences (PRD §6.3). Reads use Server Components, mutations use Server Actions, and Route Handlers serve the cron trigger and the email-token cancel endpoint. Data lives in PostgreSQL via Drizzle. Staff authenticate with Better Auth; patients never log in and act through one-time signed email tokens. Email goes out through Resend + React Email.

```
Patient (browser) ──► /book, /reschedule/[token], /api/appointments/[id]/cancel ──┐
Staff (browser)   ──► /staff/login, /staff/schedule, /staff/reception ───────────┤
Cron trigger      ──► /api/cron/reminders (CRON_SECRET) ─────────────────────────┤
                                                                                 ▼
                                   Next.js app (RSC reads · Server Actions · Route Handlers)
                                        │                    │
                                        ▼                    ▼
                               PostgreSQL (Drizzle)     Resend + React Email
```

### Web Frontend

| Component | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Booking wizard `/book` | Multi-step booking: doctor + service → date → slot → patient details → confirm | PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-001, §Clinic.3 |
| Reschedule page `/reschedule/[token]` | Show current appointment, pick new slot, confirm | PRD F-U-004, §Clinic.3 |
| Cancel confirmation page | Confirm the cancel, then show the result | PRD F-U-002 |
| Staff login `/staff/login` | Staff sign-in, issues session | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Doctor schedule `/staff/schedule` | Today + week view, own column only, appointment details | PRD F-S-001, §Clinic.3 |
| Reception board `/staff/reception` | All doctors' schedules + reception data table; reassign / override / create | PRD F-S-002, §Clinic.3 |
| Staff shell | Branded header (logo + nav) + footer, sidebar for staff | PRD §8.1, §8.3 |

**Tech stack (Web Frontend)**: shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4 (OKLCH tokens, next-themes dark mode), react-hook-form + Zod + shadcn Form, TanStack Table, Schedule-X, shadcn Charts (Recharts), lucide icons (PRD §6.3, §8.1).

#### UI components & patterns

| Component | Purpose | Variants | Source |
|-----------|---------|----------|--------|
| shadcn Blocks `dashboard-01` + sidebar block | Staff shell | — | PRD §8.1 |
| Calendar (react-day-picker) | Date picking | past / weekend / out-of-hours disabled | PRD §8.1, F-U-001 |
| Multi-step Form | Booking wizard — one `<form>`, one RHF instance, per-step Zod via `trigger(fields)` | per step | PRD §8.1 |
| Data table (TanStack Table + shadcn data-table) | Reception queue, patient list | — | PRD §8.1 |
| Schedule-X resource view | Doctor schedule grid (rows = doctors, columns = time) | own column (doctor) / all columns (receptionist) | PRD §8.1, F-S-001, F-S-002 |
| Status badge | Appointment status as text + icon + color | `booked \| cancelled \| completed` | PRD §8.2 |
| Origin UI / Kibo UI extensions | Application components beyond shadcn core | — | PRD §8.1 |

### Backend

| Component | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Availability logic | 15-min slots 09:00–17:00, lunch 12:00–13:00 excluded, narrowed by doctor `working_hours`, taken slots excluded | PRD BR-001, F-U-001 |
| Booking / reschedule mutations | Transactional insert; atomic slot swap | PRD BR-002, F-U-004, AC-006 |
| One-time signed token | Authorizes patient cancel/reschedule | PRD §3, §6.3, §Clinic.3 |
| Due-reminder sweep | Selects due, unsent reminders; sends; flips `reminder_sent` | PRD §6.3, F-U-003, AC-004 |
| Role scoping | Doctor → own; receptionist → all; enforced at every layer | PRD AC-005 |

**Tech stack (Backend)**: Next.js 16 Server Actions + Route Handlers, PostgreSQL, Drizzle + drizzle-kit, Better Auth (DB-backed sessions, Drizzle adapter, RBAC), Zod v4; Bun 1.3.x as package manager/test runner, Node as self-host server runtime (PRD §6.3).

### Integrations

| Component | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Resend + React Email | Confirmation, reminder, reschedule and reassignment emails (SPF/DKIM/DMARC on the sending domain) | PRD §6.3, F-U-001, F-U-003, F-U-004, F-S-002 |
| Cron trigger | Calls the reminder sweep — Vercel Cron (Vercel) or `croner` in a persistent Bun process (self-host); target open: OQ-AR-1 | PRD §6.3 |

### API contracts

| Surface | Type | Route | Purpose | Auth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Booking wizard | RSC page + Server Action | `/book` | Create `online` appointment | public (rate-limited — limit: OQ-AR-2) | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Cancel via token | Route Handler | `/api/appointments/[id]/cancel` (+ token) | Cancel appointment, free slot (method: OQ-AR-3) | one-time signed token | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Reschedule via token | RSC page + Server Action | `/reschedule/[token]` | Atomic slot swap | one-time signed token | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Doctor schedule | RSC page | `/staff/schedule` | Own schedule | Better Auth (`doctor`) | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Reception board | RSC page | `/staff/reception` | All schedules + board actions | Better Auth (`receptionist`) | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Staff login | RSC page + Server Action | `/staff/login` | Issue staff session | public → session | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Reminder cron | Route Handler | `/api/cron/reminders` | Run due-reminder sweep | `CRON_SECRET` | PRD §Clinic.3 |

Error responses are not specified in the PRD beyond AC-002 (concurrent insert fails) — patient-facing handling: OQ-FL-7.

### Sources

- PRD §6.3, §8.1, §Clinic.1, §Clinic.3, §Clinic.5

### Out of Scope

- Multi-clinic, payments, SMS, medical records, recurring appointments, patient accounts (PRD §7).

## Decisions

> ADR-lite — every entry is stated by the PRD. Anything the PRD leaves open is an Open Question in constraints.md.

### D-001: Next.js 16 App Router as a full-stack app

One app for patients and staff. **Decision**: Server Components for reads, Server Actions for mutations, Route Handlers for the cron trigger and the email-token cancel/reschedule endpoints. **Consequences**: no separate backend service; server-side logic sits in the Next.js app. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Framework.

### D-002: Bun 1.3.x as package manager and test runner

**Decision**: Bun is the package manager and test runner everywhere; Bun-as-production-server is beta — Bun-on-Vercel beta on Vercel, otherwise Node as the self-hosted server runtime (pin-and-watch). **Consequences**: runtime posture depends on the deployment target (OQ-AR-1); PRD also names Vitest for unit tests (OQ-AR-5). **Source**: PRD §6.3 Runtime.

**Decision**: PostgreSQL is the database; Drizzle is the ORM and drizzle-kit runs migrations. **Consequences**: the double-booking guard (D-007) lives in the schema. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Database.

**Decision**: Resend sends, React Email renders; SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured on the sending domain. **Consequences**: email-only notifications (no SMS, PRD §7). **Source**: PRD §6.3 Email.

**Decision**: a persisted sweep (not per-appointment in-memory timers), triggered by Vercel Cron on Vercel or `croner` in a persistent Bun process when self-hosted. **Consequences**: sweep must be idempotent (AC-004); trigger choice follows OQ-AR-1. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Scheduled reminders.

> Online appointment booking for one small clinic: patients self-book, reschedule and cancel without calling; doctors and receptionists manage the daily schedule.

**Scope**: Clinic Web App (`CLINIC`)
**PICs**: Engineering Lead, Design Lead
**Priority**: 1 (delivery sequencing hint)
**PRD source**: `PRD/prd-clinic.md` (sha256: `34b026c22edebce30d2d5853edc5f8a58a3349891df4f96e482ed9f1e6465d0a`)

**Sibling scopes**: none — single-scope PRD. **Locked contracts published / consumed**: none (PRD `cross_scope_dependencies: []`).

> Generic AI-consumer protocol (how to read this vault, halt handling, standard terms): `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md`.

## Phase context

**Phase:** 1 of 1

**Project type:** single-phase

## Overview

> **TL;DR**: What the clinic booking product is, who uses it, and how success is measured · PO, architect, QA · read first.

### Product

A web app for one clinic (5 doctors, ~50 appointments/day) where patients book, reschedule and cancel appointments online, and staff see and manage the daily schedule. Automated email reminders 24 hours ahead aim to cut no-shows. The UI must be accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA).

### Target users / personas

- **Patient**: books, reschedules and cancels their own appointments; no login — cancel/reschedule via a one-time email token (PRD §3).
- **Doctor**: staff role; views their own schedule (PRD §3).
- **Receptionist**: staff role; views all schedules, manages conflicts, creates walk-in/phone appointments (PRD §3).
- **Product Owner / clinic staff**: own rollout and success metrics (PRD §3).

### Problem

Bookings happen by phone (~5 min of staff time each) and the no-show rate is 18%. Patients cannot self-serve, and staff lack an at-a-glance schedule (PRD §1, §2).

### Success criteria

- ≥ 50% of appointments booked online within 3 months, measured via `booking_channel` (PRD §2, §9, BR-006).
- No-show rate < 10% within 3 months, baseline 18% (PRD §2, §9) — measurement method open: OQ-OV-2.
- Median staff time per booking < 30 s, down from ~5 min (PRD §2, §9) — measurement method open: OQ-OV-3.
- WCAG 2.2 AA across the UI (PRD §2, §6.1).

### Sources

- PRD §1, §2, §3, §9

### Out of Scope

- Multi-clinic support · payment processing (price display only) · SMS reminders · patient medical records · recurring appointments · multi-language UI (English only) · patient login/accounts (PRD §7).

## Architecture

> **TL;DR**: One Next.js full-stack app — public patient surfaces, role-gated staff surfaces, a reminder cron endpoint, Postgres storage, email integration · architect, devs · read before designing any unit.

### System overview

A single Next.js 16 (App Router) app serves both audiences (PRD §6.3). Reads use Server Components, mutations use Server Actions, and Route Handlers serve the cron trigger and the email-token cancel endpoint. Data lives in PostgreSQL via Drizzle. Staff authenticate with Better Auth; patients never log in and act through one-time signed email tokens. Email goes out through Resend + React Email.

```
Patient (browser) ──► /book, /reschedule/[token], /api/appointments/[id]/cancel ──┐
Staff (browser)   ──► /staff/login, /staff/schedule, /staff/reception ───────────┤

                                        │                    │
```

# Data Model

> **TL;DR**: Four entities — Staff, Patient, Service, Appointment — with the DB-level double-booking guard · BE dev, architect, QA · read before any schema or query work.

## Entities (DBML)

Field names and enum values are from PRD §Clinic.4. The PRD does not state column types or nullability; types below are the plainest fit for each named field, and the primary-key type is open (OQ-DM-6).

```dbml
Enum staff_role {
  doctor
  receptionist
}

Enum appointment_status {
  booked
  cancelled
  completed
}

Enum booking_channel {
  online
  staff
}

// Purpose: Clinic staff account (doctor or receptionist); owned by Better Auth's schema via the Drizzle adapter
Table staff {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  name varchar
  email varchar
  password_hash varchar
  role staff_role
  specialty varchar [note: 'doctors only']
  working_hours varchar [note: 'doctors only; narrows BR-001 global hours; format open — OQ-DM-2']
  created_at timestamp
}

// Purpose: Person who books an appointment (no login; identified by the details they enter)
Table patient {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  name varchar
  email varchar
  phone varchar
  created_at timestamp
}

// Purpose: Visit type offered by the clinic (consultation, follow-up, vaccination) with a display-only price
Table service {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  name varchar
  duration_minutes int [note: 'relation to 15-min slots open — OQ-DM-1']
  price decimal [note: 'display only, never billed (BR-005); currency/format open — OQ-DM-5']
}

// Purpose: A scheduled patient visit with a doctor; one booked appointment per doctor per start time
Table appointment {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  patient_id varchar [ref: > patient.id]
  doctor_id varchar [ref: > staff.id, note: 'staff row with role = doctor']
  service_id varchar [ref: > service.id]
  start_time timestamp
  end_time timestamp
  status appointment_status [note: 'who sets completed — OQ-DM-3']
  reason_for_visit text
  booking_channel booking_channel [note: 'online = patient, staff = receptionist (BR-006)']
  reminder_at timestamp [note: 'when the 24 h reminder is due (BR-003)']
  reminder_sent boolean [note: 'flips true exactly once (AC-004)']
  created_at timestamp
  updated_at timestamp

  indexes {
    (doctor_id, start_time) [unique, note: 'partial — WHERE status = booked (BR-002)']
  }
}
```

## Constraints

- **Uniqueness**: `appointment(doctor_id, start_time)` unique where `status = booked`; the insert runs in a transaction so concurrent bookings of the same slot cannot both succeed (PRD BR-002, §Clinic.4, AC-002).
- **Slot release**: setting `status = cancelled` frees the slot immediately — the partial unique index no longer covers the row (PRD BR-002, AC-003).
- **Reschedule**: freeing the old slot and booking the new one happens atomically (PRD F-U-004, AC-006).
- **Reminder idempotency**: `reminder_sent` goes `false → true` once per appointment; a re-run sweep never re-sends (PRD AC-004).
- **Channel**: every appointment carries `booking_channel` (PRD BR-006).
- **Indexes**: appointment lookup must meet < 200 ms median (PRD §6.2) — index design beyond the unique index is left to implementation.

---

## Sources

- PRD §Clinic.4 Data Model · BR-002, BR-003, BR-005, BR-006 · AC-002, AC-003, AC-004, AC-006 · §6.2

## Out of Scope

- Patient medical records (PRD §7).
- Payment / billing records (PRD BR-005, §7).
- Multi-clinic tenancy (PRD §7).

Field names and enum values are from PRD §Clinic.4. The PRD does not state column types or nullability; types below are the plainest fit for each named field, and the primary-key type is open (OQ-DM-6).

```dbml
Enum staff_role {
  doctor
  receptionist
}

Enum appointment_status {
  booked
  cancelled
  completed
}

Enum booking_channel {
  online
  staff
}

// Purpose: Clinic staff account (doctor or receptionist); owned by Better Auth's schema via the Drizzle adapter
Table staff {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  name varchar
  email varchar
  password_hash varchar
  role staff_role
  specialty varchar [note: 'doctors only']
  working_hours varchar [note: 'doctors only; narrows BR-001 global hours; format open — OQ-DM-2']
  created_at timestamp
}

// Purpose: Person who books an appointment (no login; identified by the details they enter)
Table patient {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  name varchar
  email varchar
  phone varchar
  created_at timestamp
}

// Purpose: Visit type offered by the clinic (consultation, follow-up, vaccination) with a display-only price
Table service {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  name varchar
  duration_minutes int [note: 'relation to 15-min slots open — OQ-DM-1']
  price decimal [note: 'display only, never billed (BR-005); currency/format open — OQ-DM-5']
}

// Purpose: A scheduled patient visit with a doctor; one booked appointment per doctor per start time
Table appointment {
  id varchar [pk, note: 'key type open — OQ-DM-6']
  patient_id varchar [ref: > patient.id]
  doctor_id varchar [ref: > staff.id, note: 'staff row with role = doctor']
  service_id varchar [ref: > service.id]
  start_time timestamp
  end_time timestamp
  status appointment_status [note: 'who sets completed — OQ-DM-3']
  reason_for_visit text
  booking_channel booking_channel [note: 'online = patient, staff = receptionist (BR-006)']
  reminder_at timestamp [note: 'when the 24 h reminder is due (BR-003)']
  reminder_sent boolean [note: 'flips true exactly once (AC-004)']
  created_at timestamp
  updated_at timestamp

  indexes {
    (doctor_id, start_time) [unique, note: 'partial — WHERE status = booked (BR-002)']
  }
}
```

## Constraints

- **Uniqueness**: `appointment(doctor_id, start_time)` unique where `status = booked`; the insert runs in a transaction so concurrent bookings of the same slot cannot both succeed (PRD BR-002, §Clinic.4, AC-002).
- **Slot release**: setting `status = cancelled` frees the slot immediately — the partial unique index no longer covers the row (PRD BR-002, AC-003).
- **Reschedule**: freeing the old slot and booking the new one happens atomically (PRD F-U-004, AC-006).
- **Reminder idempotency**: `reminder_sent` goes `false → true` once per appointment; a re-run sweep never re-sends (PRD AC-004).
- **Channel**: every appointment carries `booking_channel` (PRD BR-006).
- **Indexes**: appointment lookup must meet < 200 ms median (PRD §6.2) — index design beyond the unique index is left to implementation.

---

## Sources

- PRD §Clinic.4 Data Model · BR-002, BR-003, BR-005, BR-006 · AC-002, AC-003, AC-004, AC-006 · §6.2

## Out of Scope

- Patient medical records (PRD §7).
- Payment / billing records (PRD BR-005, §7).
- Multi-clinic tenancy (PRD §7).

# Flows

> **TL;DR**: Patient flows (book, cancel, reminder, reschedule), staff flows (doctor schedule, reception), and the cross-cutting role-scoping flow, each with a Definition of Done · devs, QA, UI/UX · read before building or testing a flow.

> Flow IDs keep the PRD's numbering for traceability: in this vault `F-S-` marks the PRD's **staff** flows (PRD §Clinic.1), not backend-only flows.

---

## User flows (web — patient)

### F-U-001: Patient books appointment

**Actor / Trigger**: Patient, on `/book` (public, rate-limited).

**Flow**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S1["Patient opens /book (multi-step wizard)"] --> S2["Pick doctor + service type (consultation / follow-up / vaccination)"]
    S2 --> S3["Pick a date — Calendar shows the doctor's availability; past, weekend and out-of-hours days disabled"]
    S3 --> S4["Pick a 15-min slot between 09:00 and 17:00; 12:00–13:00 lunch has no slots; taken slots hidden"]
    S4 --> S5["Enter name, email, phone, reason for visit — validated on client and server"]
    S5 --> S6["Patient confirms the booking"]
    S6 --> TX{"Transactional insert — slot still free for this doctor + start time?"}
    TX -- "yes" --> OK["Appointment saved: status booked, booking_channel online"]
    OK --> EM["Email: booking details + cancel/reschedule link (one-time signed token)"]
    EM --> Done(["Success message announced via aria-live"])
    TX -- "no" --> Fail(["Insert fails on the unique constraint — patient-facing handling: OQ-FL-7"])
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] Booking a free slot creates an appointment with `status = booked` and `booking_channel = online` (AC-001).
- [ ] A confirmation email with details and a cancel/reschedule link is sent (AC-001, F-U-001 step 7).
- [ ] The slot picker hides taken slots, and a concurrent insert for the same doctor + start time fails at the database (AC-002).
- [ ] Past dates, weekends, out-of-hours times and 12:00–13:00 cannot be picked; a doctor's `working_hours` narrows the choices (BR-001).
- [ ] Name, email, phone and reason for visit are validated on client and server (F-U-001 step 5).
- [ ] The flow works at 375 px wide and the success message uses `role="status"` / `aria-live` (NFR-001, §8.4).

**Source**: PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-001, BR-001, BR-002, BR-006, AC-001, AC-002, §Clinic.3

---

### F-U-002: Patient cancels appointment

**Actor / Trigger**: Patient clicks the cancellation link in an email.

**Flow**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    L["Patient clicks the cancellation link (one-time signed token)"] --> V{"Token valid for this appointment?"}
    V -- "no" --> Inv(["Invalid, used or expired token — handling: OQ-FL-6"])
    V -- "yes" --> Ask["System asks the patient to confirm the cancellation"]
    Ask --> C["Status set to cancelled; slot freed immediately"]
    C --> P(["Cancellation result page shown"])
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] Cancelling via the email token sets `status = cancelled` and frees the slot (AC-003).
- [ ] The patient must confirm before the cancel happens (F-U-002 step 2).
- [ ] The freed slot is immediately bookable again (BR-002).
- [ ] A result page is shown after the cancel (F-U-002 step 4).

**Source**: PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-002, BR-002, AC-003, §Clinic.3

---

### F-U-003: Patient receives reminder

**Actor / Trigger**: Scheduled trigger calls `/api/cron/reminders` with `CRON_SECRET`; the DB-backed sweep runs.

**Flow**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    T(["Cron trigger calls /api/cron/reminders"]) --> A{"CRON_SECRET valid?"}
    A -- "no" --> D(["Request refused, nothing sent"])
    A -- "yes" --> Q["Find appointments: status booked, reminder_sent false, reminder due"]
    Q --> S["Send reminder email: details + cancel/reschedule link"]
    S --> F["Set reminder_sent = true for each sent appointment"]
    F --> H(["Appointments not cancelled by start time stay booked (held as confirmed)"])
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] A reminder fires 24 h ± 5 min before `start_time` for non-cancelled appointments (AC-004, F-U-003 step 1).
- [ ] Each appointment gets exactly one reminder: `reminder_sent` flips true and a re-run sweep sends nothing new (AC-004).
- [ ] The reminder includes appointment details and the cancel/reschedule link (BR-003, F-U-003 step 2).
- [ ] Reminder email is delivered within 5 minutes of its scheduled send time (NFR-003).
- [ ] Calls without a valid `CRON_SECRET` send nothing (§Clinic.3).
- [ ] No per-appointment in-memory timers are used (§6.3).

**Source**: PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-003, BR-003, BR-004, AC-004, NFR-003, §6.3, §Clinic.3

---

### F-U-004: Patient reschedules appointment

**Actor / Trigger**: Patient clicks the reschedule link (same one-time token) in an email.

**Flow**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    L["Patient clicks the reschedule link (same one-time token)"] --> P["/reschedule/[token] shows the current appointment"]
    P --> N["Patient picks a new available slot (slot rules of BR-001)"]
    N --> C["Patient confirms the new slot"]
    C --> TX{"Atomic swap — new slot still free?"}
    TX -- "yes" --> OK["Old slot freed and new slot booked in one transaction"]
    OK --> E(["Confirmation email re-sent"])
    TX -- "no" --> X(["Swap fails, original booking unchanged — patient-facing handling: OQ-FL-7"])
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] Rescheduling frees the old slot and books the new one atomically, with no double-booking (AC-006).
- [ ] The page shows the current appointment before the patient picks a new slot (F-U-004 step 2).
- [ ] A new confirmation email is sent after the change (F-U-004 step 3).

**Source**: PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-004, BR-001, BR-002, AC-006, §Clinic.3

---

## Staff flows

### F-S-001: Doctor views schedule

**Actor / Trigger**: Doctor signs in (Better Auth, role `doctor`).

**Flow**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    L["Doctor signs in at /staff/login (role doctor)"] --> S["/staff/schedule — today + week view, Schedule-X resource view, own column only"]
    S --> D["Doctor opens one appointment"]
    D --> Det(["Details: patient name, reason for visit"])
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] A doctor sees only their own appointments (AC-005).
- [ ] Today and week views are available (F-S-001 step 2).
- [ ] Appointment details show patient name and reason for visit (F-S-001 step 3).
- [ ] `/staff/schedule` requires a signed-in `doctor` (§Clinic.3).

**Source**: PRD §Clinic.1 F-S-001, AC-005, §Clinic.3

---

### F-S-002: Receptionist manages conflicts

**Actor / Trigger**: Receptionist signs in (role `receptionist`).

**Flow**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    L["Receptionist signs in (role receptionist)"] --> R["/staff/reception — all doctors' schedules (Schedule-X, all columns) + reception board (data table)"]
    R --> A{"Which action?"}
    A -- "reassign" --> RA["Move an appointment to a different doctor"]
    RA --> N(["Patient notification email sent"])
    A -- "emergency walk-in" --> OV(["Book outside slot times via override — rules: OQ-FL-4"])
    A -- "walk-in / phone" --> CR(["Create appointment with booking_channel staff"])
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] A receptionist sees every doctor's schedule plus the reception board (AC-005, F-S-002 step 2).
- [ ] Reassigning an appointment to another doctor sends the patient a notification email (F-S-002 step 3).
- [ ] The receptionist can place an emergency walk-in outside slot times (F-S-002 step 4).
- [ ] Appointments created by staff record `booking_channel = staff` (F-S-002 step 5, BR-006).
- [ ] `/staff/reception` requires a signed-in `receptionist` (§Clinic.3).

**Source**: PRD §Clinic.1 F-S-002, BR-006, AC-005, §Clinic.3

---

## Cross-cutting flows

### F-C-001: Role-scoped access across layers

**Actor**: Any visitor (patient or staff).
**Layers involved**: route guard (proxy/middleware), data loading (Server Components), mutations (Server Actions), UI.

**Flow with handoff points**:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph EDGE["Route guard (proxy / middleware)"]
        G1{"Route public? (/book, /reschedule/[token], cancel handler, /staff/login)"}
        G2["Staff route: require session with matching role"]
    end
    subgraph RSC["Data loading (Server Components)"]
        R1["Scope query by role: doctor → own appointments; receptionist → all"]
    end
    subgraph SA["Mutations (Server Actions)"]
        A1["Re-check session + role before every write"]
    end
    subgraph UI["UI"]
        U1["Render only permitted columns and actions"]
    end
    G1 -- "no" --> G2
    G2 -- "session + role" --> R1
    R1 -- "scoped data" --> U1
    U1 -- "mutation request" --> A1
```

**Definition of Done**:
- [ ] Unauthenticated requests to staff routes do not reach staff data (AC-005, §Clinic.3).
- [ ] A doctor cannot read or change another doctor's appointments through data loading or mutations — not only hidden in the UI (AC-005).
- [ ] A receptionist can read all doctors' appointments (AC-005).
- [ ] Public patient routes and `/staff/login` work without a staff session (§Clinic.3).

**Source**: PRD AC-005, §Clinic.3, §6.3 Auth

---

## Sources

- PRD §Clinic.1 (F-U-001..004, F-S-001..002), §Clinic.3, §Clinic.5 (AC-001..007), BR-001..006, §6.2, §6.3, §8.4

## Out of Scope

- SMS reminders (PRD §7).
- Recurring appointments (PRD §7).
- Patient login / accounts — patients act only through one-time email tokens (PRD §7).
- Payment during booking (PRD BR-005, §7).

# Constraints & Open Questions

> **TL;DR**: 25 Open Questions (2 × P1 privacy blockers) plus the stack, NFR, accessibility and design constraints the PRD fixes · architect, tech lead, PO, compliance · read before choosing a solution or triaging OQs.

## Technical constraints

- **Stack lock-in (PRD)**: Next.js 16 App Router; Bun 1.3.x (PM + test runner; Node as self-host server); PostgreSQL + Drizzle/drizzle-kit; shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4; Better Auth (staff only); Resend + React Email; Zod v4; Vitest + RTL, Playwright; Biome + thin `eslint-config-next` (PRD §6.3) — see vault.md §Decisions D-001..D-009.
- **Infrastructure**: deployment target not decided — Vercel (Bun beta runtime + Vercel Cron) or self-hosted (Node + `croner`) (PRD §6.3; OQ-AR-1).
- **Integration boundaries**: outbound email through Resend with SPF/DKIM/DMARC on the sending domain (PRD §6.3).
- **Browser / device support**: patient booking flow works at 375 px; staff views are mobile-responsive (PRD NFR-001).

## Business constraints

- **Initial scale**: one clinic, 5 doctors, ~50 appointments per day (PRD §1).
- **Regulatory**: patient personal data (name, email, phone, reason for visit) is collected and stored and must be handled per the applicable regional patient-privacy regulation — which one is open (PRD §6.1; OQ-CN-1).
- **Compliance**: WCAG 2.2 Level AA — healthcare products fall under ADA Title III / Section 508 / ACA Section 1557 expectations (PRD §6.1).
- **Payments**: price is display-only; no payment code paths (PRD BR-005).
- **Timeline / budget**: not stated in the PRD.

## Non-functional requirements

| Category | Requirement | Source |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Performance | Appointment lookup < 200 ms (median) | PRD §6.2, NFR-002 |
| Performance | Reminder email delivered within 5 min of scheduled send; reminder fires 24 h ± 5 min before start | PRD §6.2, NFR-003, AC-004 |
| Availability | 99% uptime expectation | PRD §6.2 |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA on every page | PRD §6.1, §8.4, AC-007 |
| Responsiveness | Booking flow works at 375 px; staff views responsive | PRD NFR-001 |
| Security | Public booking rate-limited; patient actions via one-time signed token; cron via `CRON_SECRET`; staff via Better Auth roles | PRD §3, §Clinic.3 |

# Project Constitution — Clinic Appointment System (CLINIC)

**Status**: Active
**Version**: 1.0
**Last reviewed**: 2026-09-10
**Sign-off**: pending — Engineering Lead / Product Team / Design Lead (PRD status: draft)

> Behavioral invariants every bolt must respect. Library/stack choices are recorded as ADRs in `vault.md ## Decisions` (D-001..D-011), not here — binding decides how they map onto the codebase.

---

## §A. Coding standards (Non-negotiable)

- A-001: Every patient-entered field (name, email, phone, reason for visit) is validated on both the client and the server with Zod schemas (source: PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-001 step 5, §6.3 Validation).
- A-002: Staff roles are exactly `doctor` and `receptionist`; appointment status is exactly `booked | cancelled | completed`; booking channel is exactly `online | staff` (source: PRD §3, §4, §Clinic.4).
- A-003: All user-facing copy is English only (source: PRD §7 — multi-language UI out of scope).
- A-004: The patient booking flow works at 375 px wide, and staff views are mobile-responsive (source: PRD §Clinic.2 NFR-001).

## §B. Security baselines

- B-001: `/staff/schedule` and `/staff/reception` require an authenticated staff session with the matching role (`doctor` / `receptionist`) (source: PRD §Clinic.3, §6.3 Auth).
- B-002: Patients never authenticate; cancel and reschedule are authorized only by a one-time signed token delivered by email (source: PRD §3, §6.3 Auth, §Clinic.3).
- B-003: `/api/cron/reminders` performs no work unless the request carries a valid `CRON_SECRET` (source: PRD §Clinic.3).
- B-004: The public booking surface `/book` is rate-limited (source: PRD §Clinic.3; limit value open — OQ-AR-2).
- B-005: No payment code paths exist — service price is display-only (source: PRD BR-005, §7).

## §C. Architecture invariants

- C-001: A slot holds at most one `booked` appointment, enforced at the database level (unique `(doctor_id, start_time)` where `status = booked` + transactional insert); hiding taken slots in the UI is never the only guard (source: PRD BR-002, §Clinic.4, AC-002).
- C-002: Cancelling sets `status = cancelled` and frees the slot immediately (source: PRD BR-002, AC-003).
- C-003: Rescheduling frees the old slot and books the new one in one atomic operation — no window where both or neither are booked (source: PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-004 step 3, AC-006).
- C-004: Reminders are sent by a persisted "due reminders" sweep that is idempotent — `reminder_sent` flips true exactly once per appointment; never per-appointment in-memory timers (source: PRD §6.3 Scheduled reminders, AC-004).
- C-005: Role scoping (doctor → own schedule, receptionist → all) is enforced at every layer — route guard, data loading, mutation and UI — never in the UI alone (source: PRD §Clinic.5 AC-005).
- C-006: Every appointment records its `booking_channel` (`online` for patient bookings, `staff` for receptionist-created ones) (source: PRD BR-006, F-U-001 step 6, F-S-002 step 5).

## §D. Anti-patterns

- D-001: NEVER use the raw brand teal `#0891B2` or green `#16A34A` as `--primary` / `--accent` with white foreground text — they fail WCAG AA (source: PRD §8.2).
- D-002: NEVER encode appointment status by color alone — always text + icon + color (source: PRD §8.2, AC-007).
- D-003: NEVER use Aceternity or Magic UI components (source: PRD §8.1).
- D-004: NEVER use bento layouts on the booking wizard or appointment detail views — clinical flows stay linear (source: PRD §8.3).

## §E. Performance constraints

- E-001: Appointment lookup median < 200 ms (source: PRD §6.2, NFR-002).
- E-002: A reminder fires 24 h ± 5 min before `start_time`, and its email is delivered within 5 minutes of the scheduled send time (source: PRD §6.2, NFR-003, AC-004).
- E-003: 99% uptime expectation (source: PRD §6.2).
- E-004: Motion is restrained — transform/opacity only, 160–220 ms (source: PRD §8.3).

## §F. Compliance

- F-001: Every page meets WCAG 2.2 AA — text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, UI ≥ 3:1, visible unobscured focus, targets ≥ 24×24 (44×44 touch), labelled inputs with in-text error identification, `role="status"`/`aria-live` for booking confirmations and slot-availability updates, semantic landmarks, full keyboard reachability (source: PRD §6.1, §8.4, AC-007).
- F-002: Patient personal data collected is name, email, phone and reason for visit, and it must be handled per the applicable regional patient-privacy regulation — which regulation applies is open (source: PRD §6.1, §Clinic.4; OQ-CN-1).
