# Clinic Appointment System — Grand Design (CLINIC)

> Online appointment booking for one small clinic: patients self-book, reschedule and cancel without calling; doctors and receptionists manage the daily schedule.

**Scope**: Clinic Web App (`CLINIC`)
**PICs**: Engineering Lead, Design Lead
**Priority**: 1 (delivery sequencing hint)
**PRD source**: `PRD/prd-clinic.md` (sha256: `34b026c22edebce30d2d5853edc5f8a58a3349891df4f96e482ed9f1e6465d0a`)
**Universal sections included**: §1, §2, §3, §4, §5, §6, §7, §8, §9
**Scope-specific section**: §Clinic

**Sibling scopes**: none — single-scope PRD. **Locked contracts published / consumed**: none (PRD `cross_scope_dependencies: []`).

> Generic AI-consumer protocol (how to read this vault, halt handling, standard terms): `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md`.

## Phase context

**Phase:** 1 of 1

**Project type:** single-phase

## Overview

> **TL;DR**: What the clinic booking product is, who uses it, and how success is measured · PO, architect, QA · read first.

### Product

A web app for one clinic (5 doctors, ~50 appointments/day) where patients book, reschedule and cancel appointments online, and staff see and manage the daily schedule. Automated email reminders 24 hours ahead aim to cut no-shows. The UI must be accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA).

### Target users / personas

- **Patient**: books, reschedules and cancels their own appointments; no login — cancel/reschedule via a one-time email token (PRD §3).
- **Doctor**: staff role; views their own schedule (PRD §3).
- **Receptionist**: staff role; views all schedules, manages conflicts, creates walk-in/phone appointments (PRD §3).
- **Product Owner / clinic staff**: own rollout and success metrics (PRD §3).

### Problem

Bookings happen by phone (~5 min of staff time each) and the no-show rate is 18%. Patients cannot self-serve, and staff lack an at-a-glance schedule (PRD §1, §2).

### Success criteria

- ≥ 50% of appointments booked online within 3 months, measured via `booking_channel` (PRD §2, §9, BR-006).
- No-show rate < 10% within 3 months, baseline 18% (PRD §2, §9) — measurement method open: OQ-OV-2.
- Median staff time per booking < 30 s, down from ~5 min (PRD §2, §9) — measurement method open: OQ-OV-3.
- WCAG 2.2 AA across the UI (PRD §2, §6.1).

### Sources

- PRD §1, §2, §3, §9

### Out of Scope

- Multi-clinic support · payment processing (price display only) · SMS reminders · patient medical records · recurring appointments · multi-language UI (English only) · patient login/accounts (PRD §7).

## Architecture

> **TL;DR**: One Next.js full-stack app — public patient surfaces, role-gated staff surfaces, a reminder cron endpoint, Postgres storage, email integration · architect, devs · read before designing any unit.

### System overview

A single Next.js 16 (App Router) app serves both audiences (PRD §6.3). Reads use Server Components, mutations use Server Actions, and Route Handlers serve the cron trigger and the email-token cancel endpoint. Data lives in PostgreSQL via Drizzle. Staff authenticate with Better Auth; patients never log in and act through one-time signed email tokens. Email goes out through Resend + React Email.

```
Patient (browser) ──► /book, /reschedule/[token], /api/appointments/[id]/cancel ──┐
Staff (browser)   ──► /staff/login, /staff/schedule, /staff/reception ───────────┤
Cron trigger      ──► /api/cron/reminders (CRON_SECRET) ─────────────────────────┤
                                                                                 ▼
                                   Next.js app (RSC reads · Server Actions · Route Handlers)
                                        │                    │
                                        ▼                    ▼
                               PostgreSQL (Drizzle)     Resend + React Email
```

### Web Frontend

| Component | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Booking wizard `/book` | Multi-step booking: doctor + service → date → slot → patient details → confirm | PRD §Clinic.1 F-U-001, §Clinic.3 |
| Reschedule page `/reschedule/[token]` | Show current appointment, pick new slot, confirm | PRD F-U-004, §Clinic.3 |
| Cancel confirmation page | Confirm the cancel, then show the result | PRD F-U-002 |
| Staff login `/staff/login` | Staff sign-in, issues session | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Doctor schedule `/staff/schedule` | Today + week view, own column only, appointment details | PRD F-S-001, §Clinic.3 |
| Reception board `/staff/reception` | All doctors' schedules + reception data table; reassign / override / create | PRD F-S-002, §Clinic.3 |
| Staff shell | Branded header (logo + nav) + footer, sidebar for staff | PRD §8.1, §8.3 |

**Tech stack (Web Frontend)**: shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4 (OKLCH tokens, next-themes dark mode), react-hook-form + Zod + shadcn Form, TanStack Table, Schedule-X, shadcn Charts (Recharts), lucide icons (PRD §6.3, §8.1).

#### UI components & patterns

| Component | Purpose | Variants | Source |
|-----------|---------|----------|--------|
| shadcn Blocks `dashboard-01` + sidebar block | Staff shell | — | PRD §8.1 |
| Calendar (react-day-picker) | Date picking | past / weekend / out-of-hours disabled | PRD §8.1, F-U-001 |
| Multi-step Form | Booking wizard — one `<form>`, one RHF instance, per-step Zod via `trigger(fields)` | per step | PRD §8.1 |
| Data table (TanStack Table + shadcn data-table) | Reception queue, patient list | — | PRD §8.1 |
| Schedule-X resource view | Doctor schedule grid (rows = doctors, columns = time) | own column (doctor) / all columns (receptionist) | PRD §8.1, F-S-001, F-S-002 |
| Status badge | Appointment status as text + icon + color | `booked \| cancelled \| completed` | PRD §8.2 |
| Origin UI / Kibo UI extensions | Application components beyond shadcn core | — | PRD §8.1 |

### Backend

| Component | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Availability logic | 15-min slots 09:00–17:00, lunch 12:00–13:00 excluded, narrowed by doctor `working_hours`, taken slots excluded | PRD BR-001, F-U-001 |
| Booking / reschedule mutations | Transactional insert; atomic slot swap | PRD BR-002, F-U-004, AC-006 |
| One-time signed token | Authorizes patient cancel/reschedule | PRD §3, §6.3, §Clinic.3 |
| Due-reminder sweep | Selects due, unsent reminders; sends; flips `reminder_sent` | PRD §6.3, F-U-003, AC-004 |
| Role scoping | Doctor → own; receptionist → all; enforced at every layer | PRD AC-005 |

**Tech stack (Backend)**: Next.js 16 Server Actions + Route Handlers, PostgreSQL, Drizzle + drizzle-kit, Better Auth (DB-backed sessions, Drizzle adapter, RBAC), Zod v4; Bun 1.3.x as package manager/test runner, Node as self-host server runtime (PRD §6.3).

### Integrations

| Component | Purpose | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Resend + React Email | Confirmation, reminder, reschedule and reassignment emails (SPF/DKIM/DMARC on the sending domain) | PRD §6.3, F-U-001, F-U-003, F-U-004, F-S-002 |
| Cron trigger | Calls the reminder sweep — Vercel Cron (Vercel) or `croner` in a persistent Bun process (self-host); target open: OQ-AR-1 | PRD §6.3 |

### API contracts

| Surface | Type | Route | Purpose | Auth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Booking wizard | RSC page + Server Action | `/book` | Create `online` appointment | public (rate-limited — limit: OQ-AR-2) | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Cancel via token | Route Handler | `/api/appointments/[id]/cancel` (+ token) | Cancel appointment, free slot (method: OQ-AR-3) | one-time signed token | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Reschedule via token | RSC page + Server Action | `/reschedule/[token]` | Atomic slot swap | one-time signed token | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Doctor schedule | RSC page | `/staff/schedule` | Own schedule | Better Auth (`doctor`) | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Reception board | RSC page | `/staff/reception` | All schedules + board actions | Better Auth (`receptionist`) | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Staff login | RSC page + Server Action | `/staff/login` | Issue staff session | public → session | PRD §Clinic.3 |
| Reminder cron | Route Handler | `/api/cron/reminders` | Run due-reminder sweep | `CRON_SECRET` | PRD §Clinic.3 |

Error responses are not specified in the PRD beyond AC-002 (concurrent insert fails) — patient-facing handling: OQ-FL-7.

### Sources

- PRD §6.3, §8.1, §Clinic.1, §Clinic.3, §Clinic.5

### Out of Scope

- Multi-clinic, payments, SMS, medical records, recurring appointments, patient accounts (PRD §7).

## Decisions

> ADR-lite — every entry is stated by the PRD. Anything the PRD leaves open is an Open Question in constraints.md.

### D-001: Next.js 16 App Router as a full-stack app

One app for patients and staff. **Decision**: Server Components for reads, Server Actions for mutations, Route Handlers for the cron trigger and the email-token cancel/reschedule endpoints. **Consequences**: no separate backend service; server-side logic sits in the Next.js app. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Framework.

### D-002: Bun 1.3.x as package manager and test runner

**Decision**: Bun is the package manager and test runner everywhere; Bun-as-production-server is beta — Bun-on-Vercel beta on Vercel, otherwise Node as the self-hosted server runtime (pin-and-watch). **Consequences**: runtime posture depends on the deployment target (OQ-AR-1); PRD also names Vitest for unit tests (OQ-AR-5). **Source**: PRD §6.3 Runtime.

### D-003: PostgreSQL with Drizzle + drizzle-kit

**Decision**: PostgreSQL is the database; Drizzle is the ORM and drizzle-kit runs migrations. **Consequences**: the double-booking guard (D-007) lives in the schema. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Database.

### D-004: Better Auth for staff only; patients use one-time signed email tokens

**Decision**: Better Auth with DB-backed sessions, Drizzle adapter and RBAC for `doctor` / `receptionist`; patients stay unauthenticated and cancel/reschedule through a one-time signed email token. **Consequences**: the Staff table is owned by Better Auth's schema; token lifecycle details are open (OQ-FL-6). **Source**: PRD §3, §6.3 Auth, §Clinic.4.

### D-005: Resend + React Email for all outbound email

**Decision**: Resend sends, React Email renders; SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured on the sending domain. **Consequences**: email-only notifications (no SMS, PRD §7). **Source**: PRD §6.3 Email.

### D-006: Reminders via a DB-backed "due reminders" sweep

**Decision**: a persisted sweep (not per-appointment in-memory timers), triggered by Vercel Cron on Vercel or `croner` in a persistent Bun process when self-hosted. **Consequences**: sweep must be idempotent (AC-004); trigger choice follows OQ-AR-1. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Scheduled reminders.

### D-007: Double-booking prevented at the database level

**Decision**: unique constraint on `(doctor_id, start_time)` where `status = booked`, plus a transactional insert. **Consequences**: the picker hiding taken slots is a UX aid, not the guard; cancelling frees the slot immediately. **Source**: PRD BR-002, §Clinic.4, AC-002.

### D-008: shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4 as the UI foundation

**Decision**: shadcn/ui (Radix) + official Blocks, Origin UI + Kibo UI extensions, TanStack Table data tables, shadcn Calendar, Schedule-X for the doctor grid (FullCalendar resource-timeline only with a paid license), shadcn Charts, RHF + Zod forms, lucide icons; avoid Aceternity / Magic UI. **Consequences**: OKLCH semantic tokens with next-themes dark mode. **Source**: PRD §8.1, §8.2.

### D-009: Zod v4 validation; Vitest + RTL, Playwright; Biome lint

**Decision**: Zod v4 for validation; Vitest + React Testing Library for unit/component tests, Playwright for E2E; Biome for lint/format plus a thin `eslint-config-next`. **Consequences**: overlaps D-002's "Bun as test runner" — see OQ-AR-5. **Source**: PRD §6.3 Validation, Testing, Lint/format.

### D-010: Price is display-only

**Decision**: services show a price, but billing happens in person — no payment code paths. **Consequences**: no payment integration. **Source**: PRD BR-005, §7.

### D-011: `--primary` is teal-700, not the raw brand teal

Raw brand `#0891B2` (3.68:1) and `#16A34A` (3.30:1) fail AA with white text. **Decision**: `--primary` = teal-700 `#0E7490` (5.36:1) with white foreground; `--accent`/success = green-700 `#15803D` (5.02:1); lighter brand hues only for fills, chart series and icon accents. **Consequences**: brand hues never carry body/label text on colored surfaces. **Source**: PRD §8.2.

## Glossary

Product-specific PRD terms (standard terms live in `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md` §Standard terms):

| Term | Definition |
|------|----------|
| Appointment | A scheduled patient visit with a doctor — `booked` / `cancelled` / `completed` (PRD §4). |
| Slot | A 15-minute bookable time block on a doctor's schedule (PRD §4). |
| Service | Visit type: consultation, follow-up or vaccination (PRD §4). |
| Reminder | Automated email 24 h before an appointment, with a cancellation link (PRD §4). |
| Booking channel | Whether an appointment was created `online` (patient) or by `staff` (receptionist) (PRD §4). |
| One-time token | Signed link token in patient emails that authorizes cancel/reschedule without a login (PRD §3). |
| Walk-in | Patient booked by the receptionist in person or by phone; may be placed outside slot times as an emergency override (PRD F-S-002). |
| Reception board | Receptionist data-table view of appointments alongside all doctors' schedules (PRD F-S-002, §Clinic.3). |
| Due-reminder sweep | Persisted job that finds appointments whose reminder is due and unsent, and sends them (PRD §6.3). |

# Constraints & Open Questions

> **TL;DR**: 25 Open Questions (2 × P1 privacy blockers) plus the stack, NFR, accessibility and design constraints the PRD fixes · architect, tech lead, PO, compliance · read before choosing a solution or triaging OQs.

## Technical constraints

- **Stack lock-in (PRD)**: Next.js 16 App Router; Bun 1.3.x (PM + test runner; Node as self-host server); PostgreSQL + Drizzle/drizzle-kit; shadcn/ui on Tailwind v4; Better Auth (staff only); Resend + React Email; Zod v4; Vitest + RTL, Playwright; Biome + thin `eslint-config-next` (PRD §6.3) — see vault.md §Decisions D-001..D-009.
- **Infrastructure**: deployment target not decided — Vercel (Bun beta runtime + Vercel Cron) or self-hosted (Node + `croner`) (PRD §6.3; OQ-AR-1).
- **Integration boundaries**: outbound email through Resend with SPF/DKIM/DMARC on the sending domain (PRD §6.3).
- **Browser / device support**: patient booking flow works at 375 px; staff views are mobile-responsive (PRD NFR-001).

## Business constraints

- **Initial scale**: one clinic, 5 doctors, ~50 appointments per day (PRD §1).
- **Regulatory**: patient personal data (name, email, phone, reason for visit) is collected and stored and must be handled per the applicable regional patient-privacy regulation — which one is open (PRD §6.1; OQ-CN-1).
- **Compliance**: WCAG 2.2 Level AA — healthcare products fall under ADA Title III / Section 508 / ACA Section 1557 expectations (PRD §6.1).
- **Payments**: price is display-only; no payment code paths (PRD BR-005).
- **Timeline / budget**: not stated in the PRD.

## Non-functional requirements

| Category | Requirement | Source |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Performance | Appointment lookup < 200 ms (median) | PRD §6.2, NFR-002 |
| Performance | Reminder email delivered within 5 min of scheduled send; reminder fires 24 h ± 5 min before start | PRD §6.2, NFR-003, AC-004 |
| Availability | 99% uptime expectation | PRD §6.2 |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA on every page | PRD §6.1, §8.4, AC-007 |
| Responsiveness | Booking flow works at 375 px; staff views responsive | PRD NFR-001 |
| Security | Public booking rate-limited; patient actions via one-time signed token; cron via `CRON_SECRET`; staff via Better Auth roles | PRD §3, §Clinic.3 |
| Data integrity | Double-booking impossible at the database level | PRD BR-002, AC-002 |

## Design system

### Tokens

**Color**:
| Token | Value | Use case | Source |
|-------|-------|----------|--------|
| `--primary` | teal-700 `#0E7490` = `oklch(0.520 0.094 223.1)` (5.36:1 on white) | primary actions, white foreground | PRD §8.2 |
| `--accent` / success | green-700 `#15803D` = `oklch(0.527 0.137 150.1)` (5.02:1) | accent / success | PRD §8.2 |
| brand teal (raw) | `#0891B2` (3.68:1 — fails AA for white text) | fills, chart series, icon accents only | PRD §8.2 |
| brand green (raw) | `#16A34A` (3.30:1 — fails AA for white text) | fills, chart series, icon accents only | PRD §8.2 |

**Theming**: shadcn CSS-variable semantic tokens in OKLCH; `:root` light + `.dark` overrides via next-themes; generated with tweakcn — Source: PRD §8.2.

**Typography**: humanist sans body (warmer than default Inter/Geist), optional serif display headers, a real type scale — families and scale values not specified (OQ-CN-4) — Source: PRD §8.3.

**Radius / elevation**: a deliberate `--radius` and a consistent shadow/border language — values not specified (OQ-CN-4) — Source: PRD §8.3.

**Motion**: restrained, transform/opacity only, 160–220 ms — Source: PRD §8.3.

### Accessibility

- WCAG level: **WCAG 2.2 AA** (PRD §6.1, §8.4, AC-007).
- Color contrast: ≥ 4.5:1 text, ≥ 3:1 UI (PRD §8.4).
- Focus and targets: visible, unobscured focus; target size ≥ 24×24 (44×44 touch) (PRD §8.4).
- Forms: labelled inputs with in-text error identification (PRD §8.4).
- Live regions: `role="status"` / `aria-live` for booking confirmations and slot-availability updates (PRD §8.4).
- Structure: semantic landmarks; full keyboard reachability (PRD §8.4).
- Status is never color-only: booked / cancelled / completed shown by text + icon + color (PRD §8.2, AC-007).

### Voice & brand (light)

- User-facing locale: English only (PRD §7).
- Brand application: move off the default neutral palette; apply brand color selectively to high-signal elements (PRD §8.3).
- Page furniture: branded header (logo + nav) and footer; width-filling composition (two-column booking, hero/empty states), not a lone centered card (PRD §8.3).
- Clinical flows stay linear — no bento layouts on the wizard or detail views (PRD §8.3).
- Avoid flashy libraries (Aceternity / Magic UI) for a clinical product (PRD §8.1).

## Sources

- PRD §1, §3, §6.1, §6.2, §6.3, §7, §8.1–§8.4, NFR-001..003, BR-002, BR-005, AC-002, AC-004, AC-007

## Out of Scope

- SMS channel, payment compliance (no payment processing), multi-language/locale rules (PRD §7).

## Open Questions

- [ ] **OQ-CN-1** [P1] [business] [conf: high]: The app stores each patient's name, email, phone and reason for visit, and emails appointment details. Which patient-privacy regulation applies in the clinic's region (HIPAA, a GDPR-equivalent, or another), and what does it require for how this data is stored and what may appear in emails? (PRD OQ-CLINIC-001, §6.1) — resolve: Product Owner + legal/compliance
- [ ] **OQ-CN-2** [P1] [business] [conf: high] [origin: flows.md#F-S-001]: Staff screens show patient names next to appointments. Should a patient ever see another patient's name in any view, and which privacy rules follow for the schedule screens? (PRD OQ-CLINIC-002) — resolve: Product Owner + compliance
- [ ] **OQ-FL-1** [P2] [business] [conf: high] [origin: flows.md#F-U-002]: BR-004 says an appointment not cancelled by its start time is held as confirmed, but the PRD leaves the cancellation window open. Can patients cancel or reschedule any time up to the appointment, or only until N hours before? (PRD OQ-CLINIC-003) — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-FL-2** [P2] [business] [conf: high] [origin: flows.md#F-S-002]: When a doctor calls in sick, what happens to their booked appointments — does the system notify and reassign patients automatically, or does the receptionist handle it by hand? (PRD OQ-CLINIC-004) — resolve: Product Owner + clinic staff
- [ ] **OQ-AR-1** [P2] [tech / recommend] [conf: medium] [origin: vault.md#Architecture]: Reminders need a scheduled trigger, and the PRD offers two setups. Where will the app run — on Vercel (Bun beta runtime + Vercel Cron, Pro tier for sub-daily cron) or self-hosted (Node server + croner)? (PRD OQ-CLINIC-005, §6.3) — resolve: see Auto-Classification Review
- [ ] **OQ-DM-1** [P2] [business] [conf: low] [origin: model.md#Entities]: Each service has its own duration (duration_minutes), but slots are 15 minutes. If a service lasts longer than 15 minutes, does it take up several consecutive slots, and how should end_time be set? — resolve: Product Owner + clinic staff
- [ ] **OQ-DM-2** [P2] [business] [conf: low] [origin: model.md#Entities]: A doctor's working_hours can narrow the 09:00–17:00 window. What does a doctor's working pattern look like — different hours per weekday, days off, one-off absences — so it can be recorded? — resolve: clinic staff
- [ ] **OQ-DM-3** [P2] [business] [conf: low] [origin: model.md#Entities]: Appointments can be completed, but no flow sets that status. Who marks an appointment completed, and when (the doctor after the visit, the receptionist, or automatically once the time passes)? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-FL-3** [P2] [business] [conf: high] [origin: flows.md#F-S-002]: Edge case: a receptionist reassigns an appointment to another doctor. Must the new doctor be free at the same time, and what should the patient's notification email say and offer (for example a cancel link)? — resolve: Product Owner + clinic staff
- [ ] **OQ-FL-4** [P2] [business] [conf: low] [origin: flows.md#F-S-002]: Receptionists can override booking restrictions for an emergency walk-in. Which rules can the override break — times outside slots, lunch break, a doctor who already has a booking at that time — and is the override recorded anywhere? — resolve: Product Owner + clinic staff
- [ ] **OQ-FL-5** [P2] [business] [conf: high] [origin: flows.md#F-U-003]: Edge case: a patient books less than 24 hours before the appointment, so the 24-hour reminder time has already passed. Should they still get a reminder, and when? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-FL-6** [P2] [business] [conf: low] [origin: flows.md#F-U-002]: The same one-time email link is used for cancel and reschedule. How long does a link stay valid, is it used up after one action (and a new one sent after a reschedule), and what does the patient see if the link is old or already used? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-FL-7** [P2] [business] [conf: high] [origin: flows.md#F-U-001]: Edge case: someone else takes the slot while the patient is confirming a booking or reschedule, and the database refuses the second booking. What should the patient see and be able to do next? — resolve: Product Owner + Design Lead
- [ ] **OQ-AR-2** [P2] [business] [conf: high] [origin: vault.md#Architecture]: The public booking page is rate-limited. What is the limit — how many booking attempts, per what (IP, email), in what time window? — resolve: Product Owner + Engineering Lead
- [ ] **OQ-AR-3** [P2] [tech / recommend] [conf: medium] [origin: vault.md#Architecture]: A patient cancels from a link in their email, and the PRD requires a confirmation step first. Which HTTP method(s) should the cancel endpoint (/api/appointments/[id]/cancel) use for showing the confirmation and for performing the cancel? — resolve: see Auto-Classification Review
- [ ] **OQ-CN-3** [P2] [business] [conf: low]: Bookable hours (09:00–17:00) and reminder timing depend on a clock. Which timezone does the clinic operate in, and should patients see times in the clinic's timezone? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-OV-1** [P2] [business] [conf: low] [origin: vault.md#Overview]: Doctors and receptionists sign in, but the PRD has no flow for creating their accounts. Who creates and removes staff accounts, and how? — resolve: Product Owner + Engineering Lead
- [ ] **OQ-AR-5** [P2] [tech / scan] [conf: high] [origin: vault.md#Decisions]: The PRD names Bun as the test runner "everywhere" and also Vitest + React Testing Library for unit/component tests. Which test runner actually runs the unit/component suite? (PRD §6.3) — resolve: scan manifest package.json scripts.test + vitest.config.ts
- [ ] **OQ-AR-4** [P3] [tech / recommend] [conf: medium] [origin: vault.md#Architecture]: The doctor schedule grid uses Schedule-X by default. Are Schedule-X's free views enough, or should budget go to FullCalendar Premium? (PRD OQ-CLINIC-006, §8.1) — resolve: see Auto-Classification Review
- [ ] **OQ-DM-4** [P3] [business] [conf: low] [origin: model.md#Entities]: A returning patient books again with the same email. Should that reuse their existing patient record or create a new one each time? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-DM-5** [P3] [business] [conf: low] [origin: model.md#Entities]: Services show a display-only price. In which currency and format should prices appear? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-DM-6** [P3] [tech / recommend] [conf: medium] [origin: model.md#Entities]: The PRD names each entity's id field but not what kind of value it holds. Which primary-key type should Staff, Patient, Service and Appointment use? — resolve: see Auto-Classification Review
- [ ] **OQ-FL-8** [P3] [business] [conf: low] [origin: flows.md#F-U-004]: When rescheduling, may the patient also switch to a different doctor or service, or only pick a new time with the same doctor? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-FL-9** [P3] [business] [conf: low] [origin: flows.md#F-U-001]: The booking form validates name, email and phone. What counts as a valid phone number (country format, length), and are any fields optional? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-OV-2** [P3] [business] [conf: low] [origin: vault.md#Overview]: The no-show target is below 10%, but appointments have no "no-show" status. How will no-shows be counted? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-OV-3** [P3] [business] [conf: low] [origin: vault.md#Overview]: The target is a median staff booking time under 30 seconds. How and where will that time be measured? — resolve: Product Owner
- [ ] **OQ-CN-4** [P3] [business] [conf: low]: The PRD asks for a humanist sans body font, optional serif headers, a deliberate corner radius and a logo in the header, but gives no fonts, radius value or logo file. Which fonts, radius and logo asset should be used? (PRD §8.3) — resolve: Design Lead

1	# Handoff Contract — Skill → Orchestrator
2	
3	When mega-sdd skills run under `--auto` (i.e., dispatched by `orchestrate-flow --deep` or `/mega-sdd`), they MUST emit a structured **handoff record** at the end of their chat output. The orchestrator parses this record to decide whether to auto-continue the chain, pause on blocker, or stop.
4	
5	This contract is required ONLY when `--auto` is in effect. Standalone skill invocations (the user asked for one skill by phrase, outside a chain) MAY emit the YAML but it is informational — no orchestrator consumes it.
6	
7	> **Precedence (anti-drift rule):** each skill's OWN handoff reference (e.g. `scan-codebase/references/halts-flags-handoff.md`, `execute-bolts/references/halts-and-handoff.md`) is the OPERATIVE emission spec — it loads with the emitting skill at runtime. The per-skill blocks below are a cross-skill INDEX for the orchestrator/consumer side; when they disagree with a skill's own reference, the skill's reference wins and the block here is the bug. Top-level field names/types in §Handoff YAML schema remain binding for everyone (the validator enforces those).
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Contents
12	
13	- [Handoff YAML schema](#handoff-yaml-schema)
14	- [Field-level schema annotations](#field-level-schema-annotations)
15	- [Per-skill expected emissions](#per-skill-expected-emissions)
16	- [Orchestrator consumption logic](#orchestrator-consumption-logic)
17	- [Anti-halu invariants for handoff YAML](#anti-halu-invariants-for-handoff-yaml)
18	- [Backward compatibility](#backward-compatibility)
19	- [Slash-command flag surface](#slash-command-flag-surface)
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Handoff YAML schema
24	
25	```yaml
26	handoff:
27	  emitted_by: <skill-name>              # e.g., generate-intent, bind-codebase
28	  emitted_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>
29	  status: completed | paused | halted
30	  artifacts:
31	    - <absolute path to primary output 1>
32	    - <absolute path to primary output 2>
33	    # ... list every file/dir this skill wrote
34	  next_action:
35	    suggested_skill: mega-sdd:<next-skill>     # e.g., mega-sdd:scan-codebase
36	    suggested_args: ["--flag=value", "positional"]  # exact CLI args to invoke
37	    rationale: "<1-sentence why this is the right next step>"
38	  blockers: []                          # non-empty (>=1 entry) REQUIRED when status=halted per halt-protocol §blocker envelope
39	                                        # (validate-handoff-yaml.sh FAILs invalid_handoff on an empty/absent envelope on a halt);
40	                                        # MAY be empty on status=completed or status=paused
41	  metrics:                              # optional but encouraged
42	    duration_ms: <int>
43	    items_processed: <int>              # OQs / claims / units / etc — context-dependent
44	    items_blocked: <int>                # number that require human input
45	  checkpoints:                          # checkpoint protocol; optional
46	    latest_step_id: <string>            # e.g., "claim-45" for bind-codebase, "wave-3" for extract-intelligence
47	    checkpoint_file: <absolute-path>    # <vault>/.internal/checkpoints/<timestamp>-<skill>-<step>.jsonl (canonical per paths.md)
48	    resume_command: <string>            # e.g., "bind-codebase --resume-from=claim-46"
49	  constitution:                         # when constitution.md exists
50	    constitution_hash: <sha256>         # of <vault>/constitution.md at handoff emission time
51	    clauses_referenced: []              # clause IDs cited in this skill's output (e.g., ["A-001", "B-002"])
52	  pbt:                                  # when properties: present
53	    properties_validated: <N>           # count of property-based tests run this phase
54	    properties_failed: <N>              # count violated; details in postflight.json
55	  mutability:                           # tier_distribution: { LOCKED: <N>, INTENT: <N>, ARTIFACT: <N> }  # aggregate over claims/units processed
56	    locked_claims_touched: []           # specific claim/unit IDs with mutability_source = kb_locked
57	    artifact_discards_proposed: <N>     # count of [ARTIFACT] items flagged for discard (user confirmation pending)
58	  scope:                                # id: <scope id, e.g., "BE">          # from vault.json scope_metadata.id (omit if legacy single-scope vault)
59	    name: <scope name>                  # from vault.json scope_metadata.name
60	    sibling_scopes: []                  # list of OTHER scopes from PRD (informational)
61	    prd_sha256: <sha256>                # from vault.json (used by downstream skills to detect PRD changes)
62	  cycles:                               # when convergence loops active
63	    cycle_count: <N>                   # how many auto-recovery cycles ran
64	    halts_auto_resolved: []             # halt types resolved via grounded recommendations
65	    halts_escalated_to_user: []         # halt types deferred for manual review
66	  replay:                               # when replay capture active
67	    snapshot_path: <abs path to .internal/replays/*.jsonl>
68	    divergence_classification: clean | minor | high | n/a
69	  starterkit_context:                   # optional; present when scan-codebase deep-scan stage ran
70	    reused: <bool>                      # true if cache hit (no subagent dispatch); false if fresh scan
71	    framework: <string>                 # e.g., laravel
72	    auth_lib: <enum>                    # mirrors §auth.lib in starterkit-context.yaml
73	    authz_lib: <enum>                   # mirrors §authz.lib
74	    ui_stack: <string>                  # short-form summary, e.g., "alpine + tailwind + sweetalert2"
75	    libs_count: <int>                   # total libs detected in §libs
76	  metadata:                             # optional; carries resolved model tiers when present
77	    model_tiers:                        # resolved model tier per named subagent role
78	      auth-extractor: sonnet            # example; actual entries depend on chain roles
79	      code-quality-reviewer: opus       # catalog default; may be overridden by CLI/project/user
80	      # ... (all roles relevant to chain)
81	    model_tier_sources:                 # auth-extractor: catalog           # catalog | user | project | cli
82	      code-quality-reviewer: catalog
83	```
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Field-level schema annotations
88	
89	Each annotation is machine-readable for the Step 6.b validation gate.
90	`(REQUIRED)` — must be present in every handoff regardless of context.
91	`(CONDITIONAL)` — must be present when stated runtime condition is met.
92	`(OPTIONAL)` — encouraged but absence is never a halt.
93	
94	### `emitted_by:` (REQUIRED)
95	
96	TYPE: string — must match one of the values in `plugins/mega-sdd/references/halt-protocol.md §halt-protocol source_skill` enum (e.g., `generate-intent`, `bind-codebase`). Identifies the producing skill.
97	
98	### `emitted_at:` (REQUIRED)
99	
100	TYPE: string — ISO8601 timestamp. Identifies when the handoff was emitted. Required even if orchestrator never uses it for routing; presence confirms skill ran to handoff-emit step.
101	
102	### `status:` (REQUIRED)
103	
104	TYPE: enum — one of `completed | paused | halted`. Drives orchestrator control-flow decision (auto-continue / surface-items / surface-blocker).
105	
106	### `artifacts:` (REQUIRED)
107	
108	TYPE: array\<string\> — absolute file paths. Non-empty when `status==completed`; may be empty when `status==halted` (skill may not have written output). Every file/dir the skill wrote must be listed; orchestrator uses to verify output and locate downstream input.
109	
110	> **Existence-checked at orchestrator boundary.** The per-hop gate (`validate-handoff-yaml.sh`) existence-checks every listed path (`os.path.exists` — file or dir) after schema validation passes. Missing path → halt `artifact_missing`. Closes finding D3-002 (silent-failure path closure). Skill authors: any path you list here MUST exist on disk at handoff emission time, or orchestrator will block the chain. Do not list speculative/future paths.
111	
112	### Pre-validation: handoff block presence in chat output (orchestrator-side)
113	
114	Before any schema check, the per-hop gate (`validate-handoff-yaml.sh` per `handoff-consumption.md §b.script`) scans the sub-skill's chat output (last assistant message) for a `handoff:` block (fenced yaml or inline). Skills emit handoff YAML **inline in chat output** (see "Emission contract" below) — NOT to a file on disk. No block, OR multiple blocks with CONFLICTING `emitted_by` values → FAIL `handoff_missing` with a 300-char `response_tail` for diagnosis (same-emitter duplicates validate the LAST block — the producer's own emission). Closes finding D3-001 (silent-failure path closure).
115	
116	**Design note:** the original design used `test -f <path>` against a path convention that no skill implemented. Skills always emit handoff in chat; the file-check would have produced spurious `handoff_missing` halts on every run. Corrected to chat-block detection.
117	
118	### Emission contract (skill-author rule)
119	
120	Every skill's `## Handoff emission` section MUST cause the skill to print a YAML code fence as the LAST assistant message it emits before exiting. Example minimal emission:
121	
122	```
123	... (skill's regular chat output) ...
124	
125	\`\`\`yaml
126	handoff:
127	  emitted_by: bind-codebase
128	  emitted_at: 2026-05-25T14:32:00Z
129	  status: completed
130	  artifacts: ["<vault>/binding.md"]
131	  next_action: { suggested_skill: "mega-sdd:generate-units", suggested_args: [], rationale: "..." }
132	  blockers: []
133	\`\`\`
134	```
135	
136	Skills MAY also write the same YAML to `<vault>/.internal/checkpoints/<ISO8601>-<skill>.handoff.yaml` for replay/audit, but the chat-output emission is the **authoritative source** orchestrator reads.
137	
138	Skill authors: ensure your `§Handoff emission` step runs even on error paths (best-effort emit with `status: halted` and populated `blockers:` array; do NOT crash before reaching it).
139	
140	### `next_action:` (REQUIRED)
141	
142	TYPE: object — `{ suggested_skill: string, suggested_args: array<string>, rationale: string }`. Required even on `status==halted` — must point to the resolution path (e.g., `resolve-oq` for binding conflicts).
143	
144	**`next_action.confidence` (OPTIONAL)** — TYPE: number in `[0,1]` or `null`. The producer's confidence that the recommended next step is correct. Promotes confidence from a prose/chat string (the iter-33 D5 gap — the convergence loop's hardcoded `≥0.80` was never a typed field) to a **typed, validator-enforced** field: `validate-handoff-yaml.sh` now type-checks it (a present value outside `[0,1]` → `handoff_type_mismatch`). This lays the F4 foundation for confidence-aware orchestration (e.g. demote auto-continue to user-review below a config floor) without the prior free-text-parsing brittleness. Omitting it never fails the handoff.
145	
146	> **Validator coverage:** `validate-handoff-yaml.sh` now type-checks the CONDITIONAL fields below **when present** (list fields: `blockers`; object fields: `metrics`/`constitution`/`pbt`/`mutability`/`scope`/`replay`/`checkpoints`/`cycles`/`starterkit_context`/`metadata`) in addition to the four required fields. Type-checks are **never required-on-absence** — a handoff that legitimately omits an optional block is not failed; only a PRESENT field of the wrong shape is. This closes the F3/F4 "PARTIAL" gap (the validator previously enforced only the 4 required fields + `artifacts`) without changing the blocking contract for handoffs that omit optional fields.
147	
148	### `blockers:` (REQUIRED)
149	
150	TYPE: array\<object\> — non-empty per halt-protocol `§blocker envelope` when `status==halted` (`validate-handoff-yaml.sh` FAILs `invalid_handoff` on an empty/absent blocker envelope on a halt). MAY be empty when `status==completed` or `status==paused` — a paused skill legitimately carries `blockers: []` and surfaces triage via `metrics.items_blocked` (e.g. generate-intent's P1-OQ pause; per §Precedence :7 the skill's own reference is operative). This narrows :40/:163 to agree with `§Status values` :249, the halted-specific source.
151	
152	### `metrics:` (OPTIONAL but encouraged)
153	
154	TYPE: object — skill-specific metric fields (e.g., `duration_ms`, `items_processed`, `items_blocked`). Consult per-skill section for declared metric field names.
155	
156	### `checkpoints:` (CONDITIONAL — if skill emits resume-capable checkpoints)
157	
158	TYPE: object — `{ latest_step_id: string, checkpoint_file: string (absolute path), resume_command: string }`. Required when skill ran to a checkpoint boundary and supports `--resume-from`.
159	
160	### `constitution:` (CONDITIONAL — if vault has constitution.md)

# Handoff Contract — Skill → Orchestrator

When mega-sdd skills run under `--auto` (i.e., dispatched by `orchestrate-flow --deep` or `/mega-sdd`), they MUST emit a structured **handoff record** at the end of their chat output. The orchestrator parses this record to decide whether to auto-continue the chain, pause on blocker, or stop.

This contract is required ONLY when `--auto` is in effect. Standalone skill invocations (the user asked for one skill by phrase, outside a chain) MAY emit the YAML but it is informational — no orchestrator consumes it.

> **Precedence (anti-drift rule):** each skill's OWN handoff reference (e.g. `scan-codebase/references/halts-flags-handoff.md`, `execute-bolts/references/halts-and-handoff.md`) is the OPERATIVE emission spec — it loads with the emitting skill at runtime. The per-skill blocks below are a cross-skill INDEX for the orchestrator/consumer side; when they disagree with a skill's own reference, the skill's reference wins and the block here is the bug. Top-level field names/types in §Handoff YAML schema remain binding for everyone (the validator enforces those).

---

## Contents

- [Handoff YAML schema](#handoff-yaml-schema)
- [Field-level schema annotations](#field-level-schema-annotations)
- [Per-skill expected emissions](#per-skill-expected-emissions)
- [Orchestrator consumption logic](#orchestrator-consumption-logic)
- [Anti-halu invariants for handoff YAML](#anti-halu-invariants-for-handoff-yaml)
- [Backward compatibility](#backward-compatibility)
- [Slash-command flag surface](#slash-command-flag-surface)

---

## Handoff YAML schema

```yaml
handoff:
  emitted_by: <skill-name>              # e.g., generate-intent, bind-codebase
  emitted_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>
  status: completed | paused | halted
  artifacts:
    - <absolute path to primary output 1>
    - <absolute path to primary output 2>
    # ... list every file/dir this skill wrote
  next_action:
    suggested_skill: mega-sdd:<next-skill>     # e.g., mega-sdd:scan-codebase
    suggested_args: ["--flag=value", "positional"]  # exact CLI args to invoke
    rationale: "<1-sentence why this is the right next step>"
  blockers: []                          # non-empty (>=1 entry) REQUIRED when status=halted per halt-protocol §blocker envelope
                                        # (validate-handoff-yaml.sh FAILs invalid_handoff on an empty/absent envelope on a halt);
                                        # MAY be empty on status=completed or status=paused
  metrics:                              # optional but encouraged
    duration_ms: <int>
    items_processed: <int>              # OQs / claims / units / etc — context-dependent
    items_blocked: <int>                # number that require human input
  checkpoints:                          # checkpoint protocol; optional
    latest_step_id: <string>            # e.g., "claim-45" for bind-codebase, "wave-3" for extract-intelligence
    checkpoint_file: <absolute-path>    # <vault>/.internal/checkpoints/<timestamp>-<skill>-<step>.jsonl (canonical per paths.md)
    resume_command: <string>            # e.g., "bind-codebase --resume-from=claim-46"
  constitution:                         # when constitution.md exists
    constitution_hash: <sha256>         # of <vault>/constitution.md at handoff emission time
    clauses_referenced: []              # clause IDs cited in this skill's output (e.g., ["A-001", "B-002"])
  pbt:                                  # when properties: present
    properties_validated: <N>           # count of property-based tests run this phase
    properties_failed: <N>              # count violated; details in postflight.json
  mutability:                           # tier_distribution: { LOCKED: <N>, INTENT: <N>, ARTIFACT: <N> }  # aggregate over claims/units processed
    locked_claims_touched: []           # specific claim/unit IDs with mutability_source = kb_locked
    artifact_discards_proposed: <N>     # count of [ARTIFACT] items flagged for discard (user confirmation pending)
  scope:                                # id: <scope id, e.g., "BE">          # from vault.json scope_metadata.id (omit if legacy single-scope vault)
    name: <scope name>                  # from vault.json scope_metadata.name
    sibling_scopes: []                  # list of OTHER scopes from PRD (informational)
    prd_sha256: <sha256>                # from vault.json (used by downstream skills to detect PRD changes)
  cycles:                               # when convergence loops active
    cycle_count: <N>                   # how many auto-recovery cycles ran
    halts_auto_resolved: []             # halt types resolved via grounded recommendations
    halts_escalated_to_user: []         # halt types deferred for manual review
  replay:                               # when replay capture active
    snapshot_path: <abs path to .internal/replays/*.jsonl>
    divergence_classification: clean | minor | high | n/a
  starterkit_context:                   # optional; present when scan-codebase deep-scan stage ran
    reused: <bool>                      # true if cache hit (no subagent dispatch); false if fresh scan
    framework: <string>                 # e.g., laravel
    auth_lib: <enum>                    # mirrors §auth.lib in starterkit-context.yaml
    authz_lib: <enum>                   # mirrors §authz.lib
    ui_stack: <string>                  # short-form summary, e.g., "alpine + tailwind + sweetalert2"
    libs_count: <int>                   # total libs detected in §libs
  metadata:                             # optional; carries resolved model tiers when present
    model_tiers:                        # resolved model tier per named subagent role
      auth-extractor: sonnet            # example; actual entries depend on chain roles
      code-quality-reviewer: opus       # catalog default; may be overridden by CLI/project/user
      # ... (all roles relevant to chain)
    model_tier_sources:                 # auth-extractor: catalog           # catalog | user | project | cli
      code-quality-reviewer: catalog
```

---

## Field-level schema annotations

Each annotation is machine-readable for the Step 6.b validation gate.
`(REQUIRED)` — must be present in every handoff regardless of context.
`(CONDITIONAL)` — must be present when stated runtime condition is met.
`(OPTIONAL)` — encouraged but absence is never a halt.

### `emitted_by:` (REQUIRED)

TYPE: string — must match one of the values in `plugins/mega-sdd/references/halt-protocol.md §halt-protocol source_skill` enum (e.g., `generate-intent`, `bind-codebase`). Identifies the producing skill.

### `emitted_at:` (REQUIRED)

TYPE: string — ISO8601 timestamp. Identifies when the handoff was emitted. Required even if orchestrator never uses it for routing; presence confirms skill ran to handoff-emit step.

### `status:` (REQUIRED)

TYPE: enum — one of `completed | paused | halted`. Drives orchestrator control-flow decision (auto-continue / surface-items / surface-blocker).

### `artifacts:` (REQUIRED)

TYPE: array\<string\> — absolute file paths. Non-empty when `status==completed`; may be empty when `status==halted` (skill may not have written output). Every file/dir the skill wrote must be listed; orchestrator uses to verify output and locate downstream input.

> **Existence-checked at orchestrator boundary.** The per-hop gate (`validate-handoff-yaml.sh`) existence-checks every listed path (`os.path.exists` — file or dir) after schema validation passes. Missing path → halt `artifact_missing`. Closes finding D3-002 (silent-failure path closure). Skill authors: any path you list here MUST exist on disk at handoff emission time, or orchestrator will block the chain. Do not list speculative/future paths.

### Pre-validation: handoff block presence in chat output (orchestrator-side)

Before any schema check, the per-hop gate (`validate-handoff-yaml.sh` per `handoff-consumption.md §b.script`) scans the sub-skill's chat output (last assistant message) for a `handoff:` block (fenced yaml or inline). Skills emit handoff YAML **inline in chat output** (see "Emission contract" below) — NOT to a file on disk. No block, OR multiple blocks with CONFLICTING `emitted_by` values → FAIL `handoff_missing` with a 300-char `response_tail` for diagnosis (same-emitter duplicates validate the LAST block — the producer's own emission). Closes finding D3-001 (silent-failure path closure).

**Design note:** the original design used `test -f <path>` against a path convention that no skill implemented. Skills always emit handoff in chat; the file-check would have produced spurious `handoff_missing` halts on every run. Corrected to chat-block detection.

### Emission contract (skill-author rule)

Every skill's `## Handoff emission` section MUST cause the skill to print a YAML code fence as the LAST assistant message it emits before exiting. Example minimal emission:

```
... (skill's regular chat output) ...

\`\`\`yaml
handoff:
  emitted_by: bind-codebase
  emitted_at: 2026-05-25T14:32:00Z
  status: completed
  artifacts: ["<vault>/binding.md"]
  next_action: { suggested_skill: "mega-sdd:generate-units", suggested_args: [], rationale: "..." }
  blockers: []
\`\`\`
```

Skills MAY also write the same YAML to `<vault>/.internal/checkpoints/<ISO8601>-<skill>.handoff.yaml` for replay/audit, but the chat-output emission is the **authoritative source** orchestrator reads.

Skill authors: ensure your `§Handoff emission` step runs even on error paths (best-effort emit with `status: halted` and populated `blockers:` array; do NOT crash before reaching it).

### `next_action:` (REQUIRED)

TYPE: object — `{ suggested_skill: string, suggested_args: array<string>, rationale: string }`. Required even on `status==halted` — must point to the resolution path (e.g., `resolve-oq` for binding conflicts).

**`next_action.confidence` (OPTIONAL)** — TYPE: number in `[0,1]` or `null`. The producer's confidence that the recommended next step is correct. Promotes confidence from a prose/chat string (the iter-33 D5 gap — the convergence loop's hardcoded `≥0.80` was never a typed field) to a **typed, validator-enforced** field: `validate-handoff-yaml.sh` now type-checks it (a present value outside `[0,1]` → `handoff_type_mismatch`). This lays the F4 foundation for confidence-aware orchestration (e.g. demote auto-continue to user-review below a config floor) without the prior free-text-parsing brittleness. Omitting it never fails the handoff.

> **Validator coverage:** `validate-handoff-yaml.sh` now type-checks the CONDITIONAL fields below **when present** (list fields: `blockers`; object fields: `metrics`/`constitution`/`pbt`/`mutability`/`scope`/`replay`/`checkpoints`/`cycles`/`starterkit_context`/`metadata`) in addition to the four required fields. Type-checks are **never required-on-absence** — a handoff that legitimately omits an optional block is not failed; only a PRESENT field of the wrong shape is. This closes the F3/F4 "PARTIAL" gap (the validator previously enforced only the 4 required fields + `artifacts`) without changing the blocking contract for handoffs that omit optional fields.

### `blockers:` (REQUIRED)

TYPE: array\<object\> — non-empty per halt-protocol `§blocker envelope` when `status==halted` (`validate-handoff-yaml.sh` FAILs `invalid_handoff` on an empty/absent blocker envelope on a halt). MAY be empty when `status==completed` or `status==paused` — a paused skill legitimately carries `blockers: []` and surfaces triage via `metrics.items_blocked` (e.g. generate-intent's P1-OQ pause; per §Precedence :7 the skill's own reference is operative). This narrows :40/:163 to agree with `§Status values` :249, the halted-specific source.

### `metrics:` (OPTIONAL but encouraged)

TYPE: object — skill-specific metric fields (e.g., `duration_ms`, `items_processed`, `items_blocked`). Consult per-skill section for declared metric field names.

### `checkpoints:` (CONDITIONAL — if skill emits resume-capable checkpoints)

TYPE: object — `{ latest_step_id: string, checkpoint_file: string (absolute path), resume_command: string }`. Required when skill ran to a checkpoint boundary and supports `--resume-from`.

### `constitution:` (CONDITIONAL — if vault has constitution.md)

Base directory for this skill: /Users/farhanriuzaki/.claude/plugins/cache/mega-sdd/mega-sdd/7.34.0/skills/generate-intent

# Grand Design Spec Generator (generate-intent)

Converts a PRD/BRD (+ Figma), a free-text brief, or a knowledge base into a 4-file layout-2 vault (`vault.md` / `model.md` / `flows.md` / `constraints.md`, + `constitution.md`, `_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md`, `vault.json`) inside a user-specified folder, optimized for **anti-hallucination dev handoff** — a downstream dev (human or AI) can implement from these docs without inventing requirements.

> **Skill instruction language:** this skill reasons in English. **Generated docs match the input language** — Indonesian PRD → Indonesian vault; English PRD → English vault. Chat prompts default to **Indonesian + English technical terms**; precedence = explicit request > the language the user writes in > Indonesian for short/ambiguous input. Tier-1 structural tokens stay English (full rules → `plugins/mega-sdd/references/output-language.md`).

## Anti-hallucination rails (THE MOAT — never relax)

> **Ground everything in the source (PRD / BRD / Figma / uploaded docs / KB). Do NOT invent.**
> **If it is not explicit in the source, it does NOT go in the body. It goes in Open Questions.**

This is the core rail and applies to every doc and to **section presence**, not just content within sections:

- **No fabrication.** No "industry best practice" insertions, no "probably they meant X" guesses, no filler. The source documents are the ONLY ground truth. If the source is silent, the answer is an Open Question — never Claude's prior knowledge.
- **Unknowns become Open Questions (OQs), never guesses.** Every ambiguity, contradiction, or gap is captured as a tagged, prioritized OQ. 50 honest OQs beats 5 fabricated answers.
- **Every claim traces to its source.** Each entity, field, endpoint, decision, flow step, and constraint cites the PRD section / Figma frame / uploaded file / KB anchor it came from. Out of Scope is always explicit (`TBD - confirm with PO` when genuinely unknown — never empty).
- **No defaulted standards.** WCAG levels, Material/Tailwind palettes, spacing scales, brand voice appear ONLY if a source explicitly contains them. Project shape is NOT a trigger; design-system sections appear only when a source supplies design-system content.
- **`--auto` never bypasses the rails.** Autonomous mode skips logistical prompts only — it must NEVER auto-answer OQs, invent field values, skip source citations, skip OQ tagging, or pretend a draft PRD is final. (Full `--auto` behavior → `references/auto-and-handoff.md`.)

These invariants hold in BOTH output modes (`compact` and `full`) and are re-asserted in the self-check before delivery.

## When to use this skill

Trigger for any of the following, **stated literally or paraphrased**:

- "Break down this PRD for the dev team" / "pecah PRD ini buat dev"
- "Spec out this feature" / "buat dev handoff"
- "Prepare context for AI-assisted dev" / "siapkan context buat AI dev"
- "Translate business requirements into architecture docs" / "Convert PRD + Figma into dev-ready specifications"
- "from this prompt" / "from a brief" / "baku dari ide" → Mode B (free-text)
- "I only have an idea, not a PRD" / "ide aja gue belum sempat PRD" → Mode B
- "rebuild from KB" / "pecah PRD ini buat AI dev" → KB sub-mode / Mode A as detected

Do NOT use to validate a vault against live code (`bind-codebase` / `detect-drift`), to evolve a vault from a revised PRD (`diff-vault`), or to resolve OQs (`resolve-oq`).

## Invocation modes (auto-detected — no flag required)

`generate-intent` has TWO input modes (Mode A structured, Mode B free-text), a KB sub-mode under Mode B, and a starterkit-aware overlay that applies to ALL modes when scan-codebase ran first.

- **Mode A — structured input (PRD / BRD / Figma).** `generate-intent ./prd.md`. Parse + decompose directly per `references/vault-core.md` **§schema + §OQ-conventions + §id-stability** (the drafting core — §constitution ONLY at Step 3.4, concurrency detail ONLY on lock contention; `vault-contract.md` is the conditional overlay: §Starterkit-binding ONLY under `--scan`, §Multi-scope ONLY when the PRD carries a `scopes:` block or `--scope` is passed). No Q&A unless the source is critically incomplete.
- **Mode B — free-text brief.** `generate-intent --from-prompt "<brief>"` (or detected when no structured path is given). Runs adaptive Q&A (≤10 questions) to fill gaps, then produces a seed-PRD + vault in one pass. Procedure → `references/from-prompt-mode.md`.
- **Mode B (KB sub-mode) — `--kb=<path>`.** `generate-intent --kb=.mega-sdd/knowledge-base/`. Consumes an `extract-intelligence` knowledge base as a legacy-rebuild brief. KB is ANALYSIS INPUT, not a 1:1 spec: vault emphasizes reengineering goals + business intent; legacy detail surfaces only where the `[LOCKED]` tier requires 1:1 preservation. A `<kb>/decisions/ADR-*.md` with `Status: accepted` (the architecture-advisor record — `plugins/mega-sdd/references/architecture-advisor.md`) is a legitimate input document: its claims enter the vault citing the ADR; `proposed` surfaces as an OQ, never a decision. Full procedure (freshness preflight, tier-aware routing, ERD freedom, Q&A loop) → `references/kb-submode.md`.

All three modes share the SAME vault contract (`references/vault-core.md` + `references/vault-contract.md`); only input parsing differs.

### Mode A / B detection rules (deterministic — no LLM judgment)

When the user invokes `generate-intent <arg>`, evaluate rules **in order; first match wins**:

| Rule | Match condition | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `--kb=<path>` flag present | **B (KB sub-mode)** — explicit; positional and `--from-prompt` ignored |
| 1 | `--from-prompt` flag present | **B** — explicit override; positional ignored as a path |
| 2 | Positional arg resolves to an existing file on disk | **A** |
| 3 | Positional arg matches glob `*.md` / `*.pdf` / `*.docx` (whether or not it exists) | **A** — warn if file missing; offer to switch to B |
| 4 | Positional arg contains whitespace OR is quoted OR is longer than 80 chars | **B** (treat as brief) |
| 5 | Positional arg has no path separators (`/`, `\`) AND no recognized extension | **B** |
| 6 | No positional arg AND a KB README is found (priority: `knowledge_base:` dir in `.mega-sdd/config.yaml` — a shared KB outside the tree, e.g. a monorepo submodule; configured-but-missing = absent, never falls through — then `.mega-sdd/knowledge-base/README.md` → `docs/knowledge-base/README.md` → `docs/mega-sdd/knowledge-base/README.md` → `old-reference/knowledge-base/README.md`) | **B (KB sub-mode)** — auto-detect, confirm with user |
| 7 | No positional arg AND no KB | CWD scan for `prd.md` / `seed-PRD.md` / `*.md` PRD candidates — at the ROOT plus one level inside dirs whose name case-insensitively matches `PRD`/`docs`/`documents`/`requirements` (the same set as derive-state's `probes.prd`; fixed set, never a repo walk). 1 hit → confirm Mode A; 0 or >1 → prompt user |

`--from-prompt` remains supported for explicit invocation; new users typically won't need it. When detection is ambiguous (Rule 3 with a missing file, Rule 6 with multiple candidates), **always confirm with the user**; detect silently only when high-confidence. **Announce any suppressed input:** whenever a higher-priority rule discards a lower-priority flag or positional (Rule 0 suppressing a co-present `--from-prompt`/positional; Rule 1 suppressing the positional), say so — "ignoring X because Y took precedence" — never drop a user's steering input silently. Edge cases (quoted single word, looks-like-path-but-missing, bare single word, flag+positional conflict) → `references/detection-and-shapes.md`.

## Flags

| Flag | Effect | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `--from-prompt "<brief>"` | Force Mode B (free-text); explicit override of detection. | `references/from-prompt-mode.md` |
| `--kb=<path>` | Mode B KB sub-mode — consume an extract-intelligence knowledge base as the brief. | `references/kb-submode.md` |
| `--phase=N` | Legacy numbered-tree KB sub-mode only (a PRD-kontrak KB has no phase lane — module = phasing unit; the flag is logged + ignored there) — scope vault generation to Phase N of `suggested-phasing.md`; writes `phase` + `phase_total` to `vault.json`; emits the §Phase context block in `vault.md`. Default `--phase=1`; out-of-range → invocation-time error/halt. Non-KB modes are always `phase: 1, phase_total: 1`. | `references/kb-submode.md` |
| `--scope=<id>` | Select one scope (BE/MW/FE/custom id, or `all` for legacy single vault) of a multi-scope PRD. When the PRD has a `scopes:` block and the flag is unset, the interactive picker fires (Step 0.9). Invalid id → halt `scope_not_declared_in_prd`. | `references/setup-flow.md` |

Auto-applied when a codebase-map exists and `--greenfield` is unset (confirm first unless `--auto`). | `references/setup-flow.md` |

## The vault output contract (layout-2, 4 files)

Mode A/B/KB all emit the SAME canonical artifact set into the user-confirmed `<OUTPUT_DIR>`:

```
<OUTPUT_DIR>/
├── vault.md             ← Frontmatter lock (vault_layout: 2 + 6 lock values + optional project_scale) + ## Overview + ## Architecture
│                          + ## Decisions (EXACT hard-header strings) + Glossary (omitted at xs)/Auto-Classification/Sources/Changelog
├── model.md             ← Entities, relations, constraints (DBML preferred)
├── flows.md             ← User + system flows (Mermaid) + per-flow Definition of Done
├── constraints.md       ← Technical/business/NFR + ## Open Questions (the ONE authored OQ home, [origin:] tokens)
├── _meta/ai-consumer-guide.md ← static copy (plain `cp` of the shipped template; never model-rendered)
└── vault.json           ← Machine-readable manifest (script-derived — `derive-vault-json.sh`; markdown stays human-authoritative)
```

- `vault.json` is the canonical structured manifest AI consumers load for fast, reliable context without parsing prose. Schema, field rules, and regeneration triggers → `references/vault-core.md §schema`. It is **script-derived via `scripts/derive-vault-json.sh`** — the script derives the structural arrays from the vault markdown (layout-2: 4 files; legacy: 7), carries at-generation pins forward, merges the authored `--patch`, and holds the `vault.json.lock` itself (exit 4 → `memory_in_use` halt). Never hand-write vault.json.
- An 8th file, `constitution.md` (§A–§F project rules), is written at Step 3.4 unless `--no-constitution` is set → `references/vault-core.md §constitution`.
- Multi-squad mode (≥2 squads) additionally emits `_meta/squads.yaml`, `interfaces/_index.md`, and `.obsidian/graph.json` → `references/setup-flow.md`.
- Multi-scope vaults tag `vault.json` with `scope` / `scope_metadata` / `prd_sha256` → `references/multi-scope.md`.

The per-file content guide (output-mode policy, readability standards, the vault.md section order + Phase-context block, the mandatory `Sources` / `Out of Scope` tails + centralized-OQ structure, and the operator-surface capture rules) lives in `references/generation-guide.md`.

## OQ classification (every OQ, every run)

Every Open Question is tagged at generation time with `category: business | tech` + `resolution_mode` + `classification_confidence`, using the auto-classifier heuristics in `references/vault-core.md §Auto-classifier heuristics`:

- **`business`** OQs → `resolution_mode: blocking` (need a stakeholder decision).
- **`tech`** OQs → `scan` (resolvable from a codebase-map; needs `scan_query`), `recommend` (Claude proposes a pick; needs `recommendation` + `rationale` + `scan_citations` + `fallback_if_wrong` — **never fabricate citations**), or `blocking`.
- **Conservative default** when no pattern matches: `category: business`, `resolution_mode: blocking`, `classification_confidence: low` (preserves blocking behavior — safe).
- Only `high`-confidence tech OQs auto-resolve downstream in `bind-codebase`; `medium`/`low` are flagged for human review in the vault.md `## Auto-Classification Review` section.
- **Memoization (re-runs / `--regenerate`):** when the vault already carries a classification for an OQ whose TEXT is unchanged (exact match against the existing `vault.json` entry), REUSE it verbatim — re-classify only new or text-changed OQs. An existing vault classification IS the record of any human correction — reuse-verbatim protects it (never silently overwrite a human-edited bracket).

The classifier runs at Step 3.5 (after the 4 files, before the self-check) and writes the classification brackets/hints into the markdown body and the JSON-only fields (`scan_query`, `recommendation`, `rationale`, `scan_citations`, `fallback_if_wrong`) into the authored patch consumed at Step 3.8 by `derive-vault-json.sh`, per `vault-core.md §Updated OQ schema`. Validation gate + halts (`oq_tech_missing_mode`, `oq_recommend_underspecified`, `oq_scan_missing_query`; `oq_recommend_citation_invalid` fires post-write via `validate-vault-oqs.sh`) → `references/generation-guide.md`.

## Workflow skeleton

Run in order. Heavy detail for each step lives in the referenced files; the **existence and trigger** of every step stays here.

1. **Step 0–0.9 — Setup (MANDATORY before any generation).** Confirm + create `OUTPUT_DIR`; set `IMPLEMENTATION_MODE` (`new` | `existing`, with `mode_migrate_after` for new); set `PRD_STATUS` (`final` | `draft`); set `OUTPUT_MODE` (`compact` | `full`); squad partition (single vs ≥2); Step 0.8 scan-aware context loading (probe codebase-map / conventions / KB; auto-route to scan-codebase if accepted); Step 0.9 scope detection + PRD filtering (picker / retrofit bridge). Full procedures, runtime ordering note (0.8 runs before 0.9), the squad-partition Q&A, and the three scope halts → `references/setup-flow.md`.
2. **Step 1 — Inventory and read.** Locate inputs (sandbox `/mnt/user-data/uploads/` vs local CWD/ask); route each file to the right reader (PDF / DOCX / MD-TXT); for any Figma URL, load Figma MCP via `ToolSearch query:"figma"` — **if no MCP and no screenshots, ask before proceeding; never invent UI structure.** Read every input fully.
3. **Step 2 — Extract before writing.** Build an internal map (product, project shape, components, entities, flows, decisions, constraints, gaps, optional design-system flags `HAS_UI_COMPONENTS` / `HAS_TOKENS` / `HAS_A11Y` / `HAS_VOICE_BRAND`). Infer + **confirm `PROJECT_SHAPE`** with the user (Project Shape Registry → `references/detection-and-shapes.md`). **Derive `PROJECT_SCALE`** (greenfield lanes only — Mode A on the PRD, Mode B on the synthesized seed-PRD): **Run** `bash $PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/derive-project-scale.sh --prd=<file>` — a deterministic structure count, never judgment (`xs` ⇔ 1–3 screens AND ≤2 entities AND ≤3 flows; zero screen evidence → `standard` — unknown gets the FULL treatment). KB sub-mode and `--scan`-overlay runs are always `standard` (script not run; legacy rebuilds are never xs). Record it as the `project_scale:` frontmatter scalar in vault.md (the deriver mirrors it to vault.json); consequences at xs → `references/generation-guide.md §Project scale xs`. Gap-handling depends on `PRD_STATUS`: `draft` may pause when gaps > 10; `final` never pauses — every gap goes to OQs.
4. **Step 3 — Generate the 4 files** into `<OUTPUT_DIR>`, per `references/generation-guide.md` — read §Step 3 + §Mandatory section template + §File-by-file content guide + §Readability standards (mandatory for all 4 files) + the constraints.md centralized-OQ structure + §Output mode policy (the ACTIVE mode's column); **the design-system content ONLY when a Step-2 `HAS_*` flag is set** (operator-surface + Design-Source OQ rules ride §Operator-workflow-UX capture). Then **Run** `mkdir -p <OUTPUT_DIR>/_meta && cp "$PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/generate-intent/references/templates/ai-consumer-guide.md" <OUTPUT_DIR>/_meta/ai-consumer-guide.md` — installs the static guide byte-identical (never model-rendered; `$PLUGIN_ROOT` per `references/generation-guide.md §Reading the templates`; the dedicated copy script was demoted to this one-liner in v7 Fase 2). Multi-squad artifacts if applicable. `vault.json` is NOT derived here — the single derive runs at Step 3.8, after constitution (3.4) and the classifier (3.5) have produced the patch content.
5. **Step 3.4 — Write `constitution.md`** (§A–§F, every clause source-cited) unless `--no-constitution` → `references/vault-core.md §constitution`.
6. **Step 3.5 — OQ auto-classification** on every generated OQ (see "OQ classification" above) → validation gate → `references/generation-guide.md`.
7. **Step 3.8 — Derive `vault.json` (single derive; MANDATORY).** Assemble the **FULL authored patch** into a scratchpad temp file — metadata + `source_documents` + `design_system_flags` [+ `design_system`] [+ scope block] [+ `phase`/`phase_total`] + the per-OQ classifier records (Step 3.5) — then **Run** `bash $PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/derive-vault-json.sh --vault <OUTPUT_DIR> --patch <patch-file>` ONCE: the script derives the structural arrays from the vault files, computes `constitution_hash` from the Step-3.4 `constitution.md` now on disk, and merges the authored patch — **never hand-write `vault.json`**.
8. **Step 4 — Self-check before delivery.** Full anti-halu + readability + output-mode + `vault.json` integrity checklist → `references/self-check.md`.
9. **Step 5 — Present.** Chat-only summary: doc + OQ counts, `PRD_STATUS`/`OUTPUT_MODE`, top blocker OQs, vault path, suggested next skill (`resolve-oq` / `detect-drift` / `diff-vault`). No "I have created…" preamble → `references/self-check.md`.

## Simplicity policy

**Default: as simple as possible** — each doc is the shortest version that still answers what its readers need; cut anything that doesn't earn its place. **Exception: `flows.md` may be reasonably complete** — flows describe step-by-step behavior with branching, error paths, and Definition of Done; completeness matters more than terseness there. Length follows content needed, not a target.

## When to push back on the user

Push-back is **conditional on `PRD_STATUS`** (full matrix → `references/self-check.md`).

- **Always (any PRD_STATUS):** Figma referenced but no MCP and no screenshots → ask, never invent UI. "Just guess the rest" → refuse politely; offer OQs instead (`final` does NOT license invention). Alien path for the environment → reject per Step 0. Output folder exists and non-empty → ask before overwriting.
- **Only when `PRD_STATUS=draft`:** missing critical sections, contradictory PRD, or gaps > 10 → pause and ask.
- **Only when `PRD_STATUS=final`:** never pause for those three; funnel missing sections / contradictions / large gaps into constraints.md `## Open Questions` with full context (PRD quotes side-by-side).
- **Design-system absence is acceptable — no push-back.** Never prompt for a Figma/tokens/Storybook source, never default to industry standards, never emit placeholder OQs for missing design-system content.

All halts emit the unified `blocker` envelope (`plugins/mega-sdd/references/halt-protocol.md §halt-protocol`); under `--auto`, P1 business-blocking OQs additionally emit a blocker the orchestrator surfaces.

Grounded (every non-trivial claim cites a source) · honest about gaps (OQs over guesses) · simple (except flows) · human-readable (reviewable by architect, PM, business owner, QA — not just AI consumers) · predictable structure · language match (output follows input language; code-level terms stay English).
